~~~~latex
% Step 4 research note: Weyl profile concentration, bubble restriction,
% and the Armstrong--LeBrun tension
% S0910A03 Agent2 (Constructor) — Explore
%
% This note extends the Step 3 near-equality analysis with three new results:
% (A) L² concentration of |W+| at the calibrated value 1/(2√6),
% (B) restriction of noncollapsed smooth blow-up limits to locally hyperkähler,
% (C) identification of a structural contradiction between the profile and
%     the equality-mechanism limit via Armstrong's theorem.

\section{The Weyl profile concentration}

\noindent\textbf{Proposition A} (Weyl profile \(L^2\) concentration).
\emph{Under the hypotheses and notation of the Step~3 near-equality analysis
(critical Ishida--LeBrun family, \(\delta_i\to0\), and the energy profile (3)--(7)),}
\[
  \int_M\Bigl(|W_{+,i}|-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6}\Bigr)^2d\mu_i
  =O(A\delta_i^2).                                          \tag{A1}
\]

\begin{proof}
The completion-square identity (Step~3, equation~(4)) gives
\[
  \frac{1}{864\pi^2}\int_M(s_i+8\sqrt6\,|W_{+,i}|)^2\,d\mu_i\to0.
\]
We write \(w_i=|W_{+,i}|\).  Since \(8\sqrt6\cdot\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6}=4\),
\[
  s_i+8\sqrt6\,w_i
  =(s_i+4)+8\sqrt6\bigl(w_i-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6}\bigr).
\]
Squaring, integrating, and using \(|s_i+4|\le4\delta_i\):
\[
  384\int(w_i-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6})^2\,d\mu_i
  \le\int(s_i+8\sqrt6\,w_i)^2\,d\mu_i
    +16\delta_i^2\,\operatorname{Vol}_i
    +64\sqrt6\,\delta_i\,\operatorname{Vol}_i^{1/2}
    \Bigl[\int(w_i-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6})^2\Bigr]^{1/2}.
\]
Setting \(Y_i=\int(w_i-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6})^2\) and using
\(\operatorname{Vol}_i\to32\pi^2A/9=O(A)\), this is a quadratic
\[
  384Y_i-C_1A^{1/2}\delta_i Y_i^{1/2}-C_2A\delta_i^2\le0,
\]
which forces \(Y_i^{1/2}=O(A^{1/2}\delta_i)\), hence \(Y_i=O(A\delta_i^2)\).
\end{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Interpretation.}
The ``calibrated value'' \(1/(2\sqrt6)\approx0.204\) is the unique pointwise
Weyl magnitude compatible with \(s\to-4\) and the completion-square residual
vanishing.  It is exactly \(\tfrac14\) of the K\"ahler--Einstein value
\(|W_+|_{\rm KE}=2/\sqrt6\approx0.816\) for metrics with \(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\).

\section{Exclusion of K\"ahler--Einstein bulk and other known geometries}

\noindent\textbf{Corollary B1} (K\"ahler--Einstein exclusion).
\emph{Any subset \(U_i\subset M_i\) on which \(|W_{+,i}|\to2/\sqrt6\) uniformly
satisfies}
\[
  \operatorname{Vol}(U_i)/\operatorname{Vol}(M_i)=O(\delta_i^2)\to0.
\]

\begin{proof}
On \(U_i\), \((|W_{+,i}|-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6})^2
\ge(\tfrac{2}{\sqrt6}-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6})^2
=\tfrac{9}{24}=\tfrac38\).
Hence \(\tfrac38\operatorname{Vol}(U_i)\le Y_i=O(A\delta_i^2)\),
giving \(\operatorname{Vol}(U_i)\le(8/3)O(A\delta_i^2)\),
and the volume fraction against \(\operatorname{Vol}(M_i)=O(A)\) is \(O(\delta_i^2)\).
\end{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Remark.}  This rules out more than the scalar-flat connector
in the familiar integral-minimizing constructions of Ishida--LeBrun~2003:
the negative K\"ahler--Einstein orbifold \emph{bulk} is also incompatible
with the Weyl profile.  For any region converging to a K\"ahler metric of
any scalar curvature \(s_0<0\), the Weyl magnitude is
\(|W_+|_{\rm K\"ahler}=|s_0|/(2\sqrt6)\), and the discrepancy from the
calibrated value \(1/(2\sqrt6)\) is \((|s_0|-1)/(2\sqrt6)\).
With \(s_0\to-4\), this is \(3/(2\sqrt6)\), giving the above exclusion.

Similarly, any region converging to \emph{real hyperbolic geometry}
(constant curvature \(-1/3\), \(W_+=0\)) has discrepancy
\(1/(2\sqrt6)\), hence occupies volume fraction at most \(O(A\delta_i^2\cdot24)
=O(A\delta_i^2)\) -- also vanishing.

\section{Bubble restriction to locally hyperk\"ahler}

\noindent\textbf{Corollary B2} (bubble restriction).
\emph{Suppose \(A\) is fixed (fixed manifold in the critical family).
Let \(U_i\subset M_i\) with \(\operatorname{Vol}(U_i)\to0\).
Then the self-dual Weyl energy vanishes:
\(\int_{U_i}|W_{+,i}|^2\,d\mu_i\to0\).}

\emph{Consequently, every smooth noncollapsed rescaling limit arising from
a vanishing-scale sequence is both Ricci-flat and self-dually flat
(\(W_+=0\)), hence locally hyperk\"ahler.}

\begin{proof}
\[
  \int_{U_i}|W_{+,i}|^2
  \le 2\int_{U_i}\bigl(|W_{+,i}|-\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6}\bigr)^2
  +\tfrac{1}{12}\operatorname{Vol}(U_i)
  \le 2Y_i+\tfrac{1}{12}\operatorname{Vol}(U_i).
\]
With fixed \(A\): \(Y_i=O(A\delta_i^2)\to0\) and
\(\operatorname{Vol}(U_i)\to0\).

For a blow-up at scale \(\ell_i\to0\): rescale \(\hat g_i=\ell_i^{-2}g_i\).
The Weyl tensor is conformally invariant (as endomorphism of \(\Lambda^2_+\)),
hence \(|W_+(\hat g_i)|^2=\ell_i^4|W_+(g_i)|^2\) pointwise.
But the volume form scales as \(d\mu_{\hat g_i}=\ell_i^{-4}d\mu_{g_i}\),
so
\[
  \int_{B_{\hat g_i}(p,R)}|W_+(\hat g_i)|^2\,d\mu_{\hat g_i}
  =\int_{B_{g_i}(p,\ell_iR)}|W_+(g_i)|^2\,d\mu_{g_i}\to0
\]
since \(\operatorname{Vol}_{g_i}(B_{g_i}(p,\ell_iR))\to0\).  A smooth
convergent limit has \(W_+=0\) on every ball, hence globally.  Combined with
\(\operatorname{Ric}(\hat g_i)\to0\) (from the Step~3 scaling argument), the
limit is Ricci-flat and self-dually flat.  In four real dimensions, this forces
holonomy \(\subseteq\mathrm{SU}(2)\), i.e.\ locally hyperk\"ahler.
\end{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Remark} (varying topology).
If \(A_i\to\infty\), the bound becomes
\(\int_{U_i}|W_+|^2\le2A_i\delta_i^2+\operatorname{Vol}(U_i)/12\).
Absolute vanishing requires \(A_i\delta_i^2\to0\).  If
\(\delta_i\sim A_i^{-1/2}\), a bubble might carry finite \(W_+\) energy;
the restriction to hyperk\"ahler then fails and more exotic bubbles could
appear.  This quantifier distinction separates fixed-family rigidity from the
uniform statement needed for the original problem.

\section{Near-equality eigenvalue structure and the Armstrong tension}

The near-equality conditions from LeBrun~2006 Proposition~3.8 impose:
in the exact equality case, \(s-\sqrt6|W_+|=\text{const}<0\), the SW spinor
\(\Phi\) has \(|\Phi|^2=\text{const}\), and the self-dual 2-form
\(\sigma(\Phi)\) defines an almost-K\"ahler form \(\omega\) in the lowest
eigenspace of \(W_+\), with the two largest \(W_+\) eigenvalues equal.

At the calibrated values \(s=-4\), \(|W_+|=1/(2\sqrt6)\):
\begin{align}
  s-\sqrt6|W_+|&=-4-\tfrac12=-\tfrac92, \tag{E1}\\
  |W_+|^2&=\tfrac{1}{24},\quad
  \text{eigenvalues}\; (\tfrac{1}{12},\tfrac{1}{12},-\tfrac{1}{6}). \tag{E2}
\end{align}
The star-scalar curvature is
\[
  s^*=\tfrac{s}{3}+2W_+(\omega,\omega)
  =\tfrac{s}{3}-2\sqrt{\tfrac{3}{2}}|W_+|
  =-\tfrac43-\sqrt{\tfrac{3}{2}}\cdot\tfrac{1}{2\sqrt6}
\]
or equivalently from
\[
  s+s^*=\tfrac{4}{3}(s-\sqrt6|W_+|)=\tfrac43\cdot(-\tfrac92)=-6,
\]
giving \(s^*=-6-(-4)=-2\ne-4=s\).
For a K\"ahler metric, \(s^*=s\); hence this saturated almost-K\"ahler metric
is \emph{strictly almost-K\"ahler} (\(J\) not integrable).

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Corollary C} (Armstrong--LeBrun tension).
\emph{If the near-equality sequence converged smoothly to a limit metric
\(g_\infty\) on any fixed critical manifold, then:}
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(g_\infty\) is Einstein (\(\operatorname{Ric}=-g\)) by smooth
  convergence of Ricci.
\item \(g_\infty\) saturates the scalar--Weyl estimate (\(K\to A\)
  reaches equality).
\item By Proposition~3.8, \(g_\infty\) is a saturated almost-K\"ahler metric.
\item By Corollary~2.5 (Armstrong's theorem),
  an Einstein saturated almost-K\"ahler metric must be K\"ahler--Einstein.
\item But \(|W_+|^2(g_\infty)=1/24\), whereas any K\"ahler metric with
  \(s=-4\) has \(|W_+|^2=s^2/24=2/3\).  Contradiction.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Therefore, no sequence with \(\delta_i\to0\) on a fixed critical manifold
can converge smoothly to a single limit.}

\noindent\textbf{Remark.}  This is not yet a complete theorem excluding
\(\delta_i\to0\): we have not established the smooth convergence
hypothesis.  What the argument shows is that \emph{any mechanism allowing
\(\delta_i\to0\) must involve failure of smooth compactness}: either
collapsing, curvature concentration, or bubbling.  The bubble restriction
(Corollary~B2) limits the allowed degenerations to hyperk\"ahler ALE models
(Eguchi--Hanson, multi-Eguchi--Hanson, or more general crepant-resolution
models), but does not exclude all possibilities.

\section{Implication for the integral extremizing constructions}

The Ishida--LeBrun~2003 extremizers use three geometric pieces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Negative K\"ahler--Einstein orbifold bulk (carrying most volume):
  \(|W_+|_{\rm KE}=2/\sqrt6\), discrepancy \(3/(2\sqrt6)\) from profile.
  \textbf{Ruled out by Corollary~B1}: volume fraction \(O(\delta^2)\).
\item Scalar-flat anti-self-dual connectors:
  \(|s+4|=4\), \(\delta\ge1\).
  \textbf{Already ruled out} (Step~3).
\item Ricci-flat gravitational instantons (ALE caps):
  these are Ricci-flat and can have \(W_+=0\)
  (hyperk\"ahler) or \(W_+\ne0\).  The profile allows
  only hyperk\"ahler caps with \(W_+=0\).
\end{enumerate}

None of these pieces can serve as the \emph{bulk} geometry of a
hypothetical \(\delta\to0\) sequence.  A sequence achieving the calibrated
Weyl profile must be supported by a fundamentally different geometric
construction --- one that is neither K\"ahler--Einstein, real hyperbolic,
conformally flat, nor anti-self-dual, but rather occupies the specific
intermediate state with \(W_+\) eigenvalues \((1/12,1/12,-1/6)\).

\section{Maximum-principle control on Seiberg--Witten data}

The Weitzenb\"ock formula
\[
  0=2\Delta|\Phi|^2+4|\nabla_A\Phi|^2+s|\Phi|^2+|\Phi|^4
\]
and the maximum principle give the pointwise bound
\[
  |\Phi|^2\le\max(-s,0)\le4(1+\delta_i)\quad\text{on }M_i.
\]
Hence \(|F_A^+|=|\Phi|^4/8\le(4+4\delta_i)^2/8\).

Both \(|\Phi|\) and \(|F_A^+|\) are uniformly bounded by the Ricci
pinching alone, \emph{without} any sectional curvature or harmonic-radius
hypothesis.  The near-equality further forces
\(|\Phi|^2\to|s|=4\) in \(L^6\) (from Proposition~3.8's H\"older
chain).  The remaining gap is between this \(L^6\) convergence and
pointwise \emph{non-vanishing} of \(|\Phi|\), which would give a
global almost-K\"ahler form.

\section{Summary and open quantitative problems}

The Weyl profile concentration (A1) provides a new geometric filter
on any hypothetical \(\delta\to0\) sequence:
\begin{itemize}
\item Known integral extremizers fail the filter (both KE bulk and
  scalar-flat connectors violate the profile).
\item Smooth noncollapsed blow-ups are restricted to hyperk\"ahler ALE
  (for fixed topology).
\item Smooth global convergence to a single limit is contradicted
  by Armstrong's theorem.
\end{itemize}

The precise open problems for completing the analysis are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Sobolev/harmonic-radius from Ricci pinching.}
  Can the uniform Ricci bound \(|\operatorname{Ric}+g|\le\delta g\)
  (with \(\delta\) small) together with the calibrated volume \(O(A)\)
  give a uniform Sobolev constant or harmonic-radius lower bound?
  If so, the smooth-convergence hypothesis in Corollary~C becomes
  automatic.
\item \textbf{Upgrade of \(|\Phi|^2\) convergence.}
  The \(L^6\) near-constancy of \(|\Phi|^2\) and the uniform \(L^\infty\)
  bound together require controlling the gradient of \(|\Phi|^2\).  The
  Weitzenb\"ock identity provides an equation for \(|\Phi|^2\), and
  Moser iteration or De~Giorgi--Nash--Moser estimates might yield
  H\"older continuity under the Ricci pinching alone.
\item \textbf{Non-vanishing of the almost-K\"ahler form.}
  If \(|\Phi|\to\text{const}\ne0\) pointwise, the self-dual form
  \(\sigma(\Phi)\) gives an almost-K\"ahler form with the forbidden
  Chern class on the critical manifold.  The zero set of \(|\Phi|\) is
  the obstruction; its codimension and topological structure are unknown
  under the present hypotheses.
\item \textbf{Phase separation vs.\ collapse topology.}
  If the almost-K\"ahler form cannot be made globally nonvanishing,
  the canonical classes must phase-separate across macroscopic regions,
  with transitions through thin topology cores.  Characterize these
  cores and determine whether the required topology can be carried
  through them while maintaining the Weyl profile.
\end{enumerate}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Files.}
Verification script:
\texttt{workspace/scripts/verify\_weyl\_profile.py}.
Step~3 base note:
\texttt{workspace/notes/step3\_boundary\_near\_saturation.tex}.
Step~3 constants:
\texttt{workspace/scripts/verify\_step3\_boundary\_constants.py} (passed).
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 5: 原研究交接

状态：Reflect（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

本步首先完整读取了 Codex 成功任务的详细文件 Sessions/S0910A03/workspace/codex_loop/work/quantitative_deficit_analysis.md，并把其精确分解与 Step 4 的 Weyl 模长轮廓、紧致性笔记结合。随后检索并阅读了 Derdziński 相关现代来源、LeBrun–Ozuch 的共形 Kähler Einstein 轨形论文、Cheeger–Naber 四维正则性、Anderson 轨形紧致性以及最新可去奇点材料。外部检索新增了 Catino–Dameno 2026、Anderson 2003、Oliveira–Sena-Dias 的 Derdziński 附录等可检索来源。

本步建立了如下可靠局部传递链。若临界固定流形序列中存在 Vol B_1(p_i)≥v 的球，Cheeger–Naber Theorem 1.13 给出坏谐和半径集合的 C(v)r^4 体积控制，从而可选取正测度固定尺度局部片。谐和坐标中的 Ricci 方程使 C^{1,α}/弱 W^{2,p} 极限在分布意义满足 Ric=−g，并经椭圆正则性成为光滑 Einstein 度量；之后可取得强 W^{2,p}_loc 收敛以传递代数曲率余量。Codex 的振幅、Hodge、调和投影和本征值缺陷在固定 A 时为绝对趋零量，故局部极限调和形式处处非零，并强制 W^+ 的最低本征值为 −1/6、其余两个本征值均为 1/12。TTCS 两项核验分别复算了谱传递和正则片提取，结果保存于 trace/ttcs/results/step5_ttcs01_verifier1_integration.md 与 step5_ttcs01_verifier2_integration.md。

TTCS 与 S0910A01 随后认为该谱属于最大本征值二重的 Derdziński 分支，局部共形于负标量 Kähler 度量而不产生非紧局部矛盾；它们还修正 Einstein–Weyl Weitzenböck 常数，标准公式 Δ|W^+|²=2|∇W^+|²+s|W^+|²−36 det W^+ 在校准谱上给出 |∇W^+|²=1/16，而非同伴脚本中的 1/24。本步向会话组发送 #223，说明正分支中 Cheeger–Naber 正则片与全局拓扑恢复的区别，并发送 #224 说明谱分支与 1/16 常数。研究笔记 Sessions/S0910A03/workspace/notes/step5_regular_patch_and_derdzinski_boundary.tex 整理了这些推导、弱 Bianchi 估计、正分支 lens 空间现象及局部共形解释。

在本步最终综合时发现，工作笔记中的“局部相容”仍依赖一个未从原始定理逐式核定的符号分支：Strategist 和 Derdziński 的常见规范形式提示 Kähler 代表可能由 |W^+|^{2/3}g 唯一确定；若对简单负本征线同样成立，恒定模长会使原 Einstein 局部片本身 Kähler，直接排除校准谱。已读来源明确推导的是 det W^+>0、简单正本征值分支，而一般两本征值结论只以引用形式出现。因此上述工作笔记在这一点是待修订的研究记录，后续不得在核定负分支规范公式前把局部相容性当作定理。与此同时，正则片提取、完整谱强制、弱 Bianchi 修正、Cheeger–Naber 测度结论及 Bochner 常数 1/16 不受这一分歧影响。

## 当时的后续问题

对这个符号敏感而会改变整个四维负分支方向的节点进行独立数学复核，并据结果重组后续研究。首先读取 Sessions/S0910A03/workspace/notes/step5_regular_patch_and_derdzinski_boundary.tex、两份 Step 5 TTCS 集成、Sessions/S0910A01/workspace/notes/step7_local_vs_global_rigidity.md，以及 Catino–Dameno、LeBrun–Ozuch、Oliveira–Sena-Dias 的实际来源。取得或直接重建 Derdziński 原始两本征值命题：从 δW^+=0 的一阶本征形式方程推导简单负本征线对应的 Kähler 代表、精确共形幂次、取向和标量曲率符号，明确谱 (−1/6,1/12,1/12) 且 |W^+| 恒定时原 Einstein 度量是否必然局部 Kähler。不要用 det W^+>0 的公式替代 det W^+<0 分支，也不要仅凭任意共形标量曲率方程忽略 Kähler 闭合方程。

同时逐项复核正则片定理的函数空间细节：Cheeger–Naber 的 tube 估计如何选出整球谐和尺度均正的子片；L∞ Einstein 缺陷如何通过谐和坐标方程产生光滑极限和强 W^{2,p}_loc 收敛；全局正则化 SW 解、调和代表、选定符号类以及 D_eig 如何在局部片上传递；固定 A 与变化拓扑时绝对误差和归一化误差分别能推出什么。若 Derdziński 规范公式产生局部矛盾，请把这些部分组合成一个严格的“单位尺度处处塌缩”定理：任何固定临界无 Einstein 流形上的 δ_i→0 序列都必须满足 sup_p Vol B_1(p)→0，并进一步分析固定总容积迫使的直径增长、覆盖空间和塌缩维数。若局部相容性成立，则转而研究完整有限体积极限上 Δf=−f/2 的积分、容量与端部衰减，以及能否借 SW 调和形式或 Chern 整数把局部共形结构延拓到闭流形上的矛盾。

完成上述核心复核后，修订本地 Step 5 笔记中不成立的分支解释，并把精确结论与来源发给 S0910A01、S0910A02。再把结果与正分支联系起来：保留 Cheeger–Naber 正则集提取，同时明确 lens 空间等相容塌缩、非塌缩曲率集中、轨形极限、覆盖上的 Einstein 构造和等变下降是不同机制。评价哪一种新结构最可能推进原题的“同一光滑流形上存在某个 Einstein 度量”，而不是只改善输入度量的局部收敛。研究仍处于 Explore；不要进入最终写作或形式化包装。
~~~~

~~~~latex
% Step 5 research note: regular patches, spectral saturation, and the
% Derdzinski boundary branch for the critical Ishida--LeBrun sequence.
% WARNING (superseded in Step 6): the weak Cotton correction below remains valid,
% but the assertion that the calibrated constant-spectrum Einstein profile is
% locally compatible is false.  The complete projector divergence equation forces
% the simple eigenform parallel.  Use
% step6_local_projector_obstruction_and_collapse_reduction.tex instead.

\section{Setting and exact deficits}
Let $M$ be a fixed critical Ishida--LeBrun manifold, with
\[
 D=A/3,\qquad
 \delta_i=\|g_i^{-1}(\Ric_{g_i}+g_i)\|_{L^\infty}\longrightarrow0.
\]
For a selected sign monopole class $a$ (fixed after taking a subsequence),
the quantitative decomposition in
\texttt{workspace/codex\_loop/work/quantitative\_deficit\_analysis.md}
gives
\[
 R_i=O(A\delta_i^2),\qquad
 \Delta_{a,i}=O(A\delta_i^2),
\]
and therefore
\[
 D_{\rm amp,i}+D_{\rm quad,i}+D_{\rm Hodge,i}+D_{\rm eig,i}\to0,
 \qquad J_{A,i}\to0.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Writing $w_i=|W^+_i|$, $q_i=-s_i+\sqrt6w_i$, and using the worker's
rescaled variables $\psi_i,\varphi_i$, one also has
\[
 \|f_i\varphi_i+6\sqrt2\pi H_i\|_2\to0,
 \qquad
 \left\||2\pi H_i|-\frac{q_i}{3\sqrt2}\right\|_2\to0,    \tag{2}
\]
where $H_i$ is the harmonic self-dual representative of $a^+$ and
$f_i\to\sqrt{q_i}$.  The curvature completion gives
\[
 s_i\to-4\quad\hbox{uniformly},\qquad
 w_i\to\frac1{2\sqrt6}\quad\hbox{in }L^2,
 \qquad q_i\to\frac92\quad\hbox{in }L^2.                  \tag{3}
\]
The rescaled spinor normalization in (1)--(2) is not the same as the
unrescaled Seiberg--Witten normalization sometimes used in the literature;
constants must not be mixed between them.

\section{A rigorous regular-patch extraction statement}
Suppose that a sequence of unit balls $B_1(p_i)$ is noncollapsed:
\[
 \Vol_{g_i}B_1(p_i)\ge v>0.                                \tag{4}
\]
Cheeger--Naber Theorem~1.13 gives, in dimension four and under bounded
Ricci curvature,
\[
 \Vol\!\left(T_r\{x\in B_1(p_i):r_h(x)\le r\}\right)
 \le C(v)r^4.                                               \tag{5}
\]
This concerns harmonic radius, not the stronger curvature regularity scale.
Choose $\rho=\rho(v)>0$ so small that the right side of (5), with $2\rho$,
is less than half a Bishop--Gromov lower bound for $\Vol B_{1/2}(p_i)$.
Then a subset of uniformly positive volume in $B_{1/2}(p_i)$ is covered by
balls $B_\rho(x_i)$ on which the harmonic radius stays uniformly positive.
Thus (4) yields positive-measure regular patches, not a uniform harmonic
radius on the whole ball or the whole manifold.

In harmonic coordinates on a smaller patch,
\[
 g_i\to g_\infty\quad\hbox{strongly in }C^{1,\beta}_{\rm loc},
 \qquad g_i\rightharpoonup g_\infty\quad\hbox{in }W^{2,p}_{\rm loc}
\]
for every finite $p$ and suitable $\beta<1$.  The harmonic-coordinate
Ricci equation is
\[
 (\Ric g_i)_{ab}=-\frac12g_i^{kl}\partial_k\partial_l(g_i)_{ab}
                 +Q_{ab}(g_i,\partial g_i).                  \tag{6}
\]
Since $E_i:=\Ric(g_i)+g_i\to0$ in $L^\infty$, (6) passes to the limit in
the distributional sense and gives
\[
 \Ric(g_\infty)=-g_\infty.                                  \tag{7}
\]
Elliptic regularity then makes $g_\infty$ smooth.  Interior $W^{2,p}$
estimates applied after identifying the smooth limit yield strong
$W^{2,p}_{\rm loc}$ convergence, enough to pass algebraic curvature
expressions in $L^p$.  One must not instead assert that $E_i\to0$ in
$C^\alpha$ or that $g_i\to g_\infty$ in $C^{2,\alpha}$; no derivatives of
$E_i$ are controlled.

For the fixed critical manifold the deficits above are absolute
$O(A\delta_i^2)$ quantities, so they restrict to every such patch.  Strong
$W^{2,p}$ convergence therefore passes (3) and the nonnegative algebraic
spectral defect to the limit.  In particular,
\[
 s_\infty=-4,\qquad |W^+_\infty|=\frac1{2\sqrt6}.             \tag{8}
\]
Local elliptic compactness for the harmonic forms $H_i$, together with
(2), gives a harmonic self-dual limit $H_\infty$ satisfying
\[
 |H_\infty|=\frac{3}{4\sqrt2\pi}>0.                          \tag{9}
\]
The limiting SW quadratic form is consequently nonzero.  The equality
$D_{\rm eig}=0$ says it spans the lowest eigenspace and saturates the sharp
trace-free $3\times3$ estimate
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(W^+)\ge-\sqrt{\frac23}|W^+|.
\]
Hence
\[
 \lambda_{\min}=-\frac16,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Spec}(W^+_\infty)
   =\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right).             \tag{10}
\]
Thus the worker's amplitude, Hodge projection, and nonnegative eigenvalue
defects really do force the full calibrated spectrum on every regular
patch to which they pass.

\section{Superseded Step-5 branch: do not use as a conclusion}
The spectrum (10) has a simple negative eigenvalue and a double positive
eigenvalue.  In the notation $\alpha\ge\beta\ge\gamma$ it lies at
\[
 \alpha=\beta=\frac1{12},\qquad \gamma=-\frac16,
 \qquad \rho=\beta/\alpha=1,                                \tag{11}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\det W^+}{|W^+|^3}=-\frac1{3\sqrt6}.                  \tag{12}
\]
This is the opposite boundary from the simple-largest, $\det W^+>0$
branch used by many modern conformal-Kaehler theorems.  In particular, the
formula $\alpha^{2/3}g$ associated with a simple positive largest
eigenline cannot be imported into (11).

Derdzinski's original local two-eigenvalue theorem instead implies that,
after orienting the simple lowest eigenline on a local double cover, there
is a positive function $f$ such that
\[
 \widetilde g=f^2g_\infty
\]
is Kaehler with negative scalar curvature $\widetilde s$.  Weyl conformal
weight and (10) give
\[
 f^2\widetilde s=-1.                                         \tag{13}
\]
Using the div--grad Laplacian, the four-dimensional scalar-curvature
transformation, $s_{g_\infty}=-4$, and (13) give
\[
 \Delta_{g_\infty}f=-\frac12f.                               \tag{14}
\]
Positive solutions of (14) are locally possible and need not be constant
on noncompact pointed limits.  Thus a smooth Einstein regular patch with
(10) is locally conformally Kaehler, not contradictory.

For reference, the standard Einstein--Weyl Weitzenbock identity in these
endomorphism conventions is
\[
 \Delta|W^+|^2=2|\nabla W^+|^2+s|W^+|^2-36\det W^+.          \tag{15}
\]
At (10), $|W^+|^2=1/24$, $\det W^+=-1/864$, and $s=-4$.
Since the norm is constant, (15) yields
\[
 |\nabla W^+|^2=\frac1{16},                                  \tag{16}
\]
not $1/24$.  The model is therefore nonparallel and is compatible with the
Bochner identity.

On a closed manifold, by contrast, integrating (14) would give
$0=-\frac12\int f<0$.  Equivalently, LeBrun's exact saturation produces a
global almost-Kaehler form, and Armstrong then makes an Einstein saturated
metric Kaehler--Einstein.  A Kaehler metric with $s=-4$ has spectrum
$(-2/3,1/3,1/3)$ and $|W^+|^2=2/3$, contradicting (8).  The obstruction is
therefore global and compact, not local.

\section{Weak Bianchi control and compactness distinctions}
The identity relating $\delta W^+$ to the Cotton tensor contains derivatives
of $\Ric^\circ$ and $s$.  The estimate $\|\Ric+g\|_\infty\le\delta$ gives no
pointwise or $L^2$ estimate for these derivatives.  What follows directly is
only a distributional bound after moving derivatives to a compactly
supported test tensor $T$:
\[
 |\langle\delta W^+,T\rangle|
 \le C\delta\bigl(\|\nabla T\|_{L^1}+\|T\|_{L^1}\bigr),      \tag{17}
\]
up to the conventional algebraic projection constants.  Any strong Cotton
or $\nabla W^+$ estimate requires additional regularity or an elliptic
identity; it cannot be assumed from pinching.

A single noncollapsed ball plus (5) produces regular patches even if
curvature concentrates elsewhere.  It does not recover the smooth topology,
remove orbifold points, control ALE bubble trees, bound the diameter, or stop
collapse escaping to infinity.  Thin regions of vanishing volume may violate
the calibrated Weyl profile at negligible total cost.  Likewise, the
unconditional Walsh argument gives $L^1$ spatial orthogonality; phase
separation additionally requires spectral/eigenline control.

The same distinction applies to the positive branch.  Myers gives a diameter
bound, but a volume lower bound does not by itself remove curvature
concentration or identify the original smooth topology.  Moreover no
universal normalized volume lower bound can hold: round lens-space quotients
have exact positive Einstein metrics and volumes tending to zero.  Such
collapse already has the desired conclusion and should be handled by lifting,
equivariant descent, or classification rather than excluded as a prerequisite.

\section{Step-6 correction}
The conclusion above was overturned by retaining the full product-rule terms in
$\delta(\omega\otimes\omega)=0$.  For constant distinct eigenvalues, projection
first along $\omega$ gives $\delta\omega=0$, and projection orthogonal to
$\omega$ gives $\omega_{ab}\nabla^a\omega_{cd}=0$; nondegeneracy then forces
$\nabla\omega=0$.  This contradicts the Einstein--Weyl identity, which requires
$|\nabla W^+|^2=1/16$ at the calibrated spectrum.  Derdzi\'nski Proposition 5
independently fixes the conformal K\"ahler factor as $(24|W^+|^2)^{1/3}$, hence
constant here.  The corrected theorem and collapse reduction are in
\texttt{workspace/notes/step6\_local\_projector\_obstruction\_and\_collapse\_reduction.tex}.

\section{Sources}
The harmonic-radius measure estimate is Cheeger--Naber, Theorem~1.13,
\texttt{Knowledge/objects/papers/1406.6534-Regularity-of-Einstein-Manifolds-and-the-Codimension-4-Conject--487f466da601--0ffa6f2917a4/object.md}.
The two-eigenvalue and conformal-Kaehler discussion is supported by
Derdzinski expositions in
\texttt{Knowledge/objects/papers/Conformal-Kaehler-rigidity-of-Einstein-four-manifolds--ee41ec8c511e--4518ab125268/object.md}
and
\texttt{Knowledge/objects/papers/Desingularizations-of-Conformally-Kaehler-Einstein-Orbifolds--8fe1aa31deb8--5b19d560b771/object.md}.
The exact monopole equality mechanism is in LeBrun's
\texttt{Ricci-curvature-minimal-volumes-and-Seiberg-Witten-theory} object.
Independent checks are saved in
\texttt{trace/ttcs/results/step5\_ttcs01\_verifier1\_integration.md} and
\texttt{step5\_ttcs01\_verifier2\_integration.md}.
~~~~

## Exact Task

Analyze the proposed local-limit route for the fixed critical Ishida–LeBrun sequence. Starting from the exact quantitative deficit decomposition and Weyl norm profile, determine precisely what convergence on a harmonic-radius patch yields for (i) the selected Seiberg–Witten 2-form/eigenline, (ii) the W+ eigenvalue multiplicities, and (iii) the limiting Einstein metric. Check whether the nonnegative eigenvalue defect plus amplitude/Hodge projection control forces the limiting spectrum (-1/6,1/12,1/12) on a regular patch. Then check the Derdzinski consequence carefully: is this spectrum locally impossible at Ric=-g, or does it give a locally conformally Kähler noncompact model? Resolve conventions, conformal factor, scalar curvature, and Bochner formula, and identify the strongest true theorem.

## Integrated Scientific Memo

# 核验结论：正则局部极限给出校准谱，但 Derdziński 不产生局部矛盾

设固定临界 Ishida–LeBrun 流形上的度量满足

\[
\delta_i=\|g_i^{-1}(\operatorname{Ric}_{g_i}+g_i)\|_{L^\infty}\to0 .
\]

固定拓扑意味着 \(A\) 固定，且符号 monopole 类只有有限多个；取子列可固定所选类 \(a\)。定量分解给出

\[
R_i=O(A\delta_i^2),\qquad \Delta_{a,i}=O(A\delta_i^2),
\]

所以 \(D_{\rm amp},D_{\rm Hodge},D_{\rm eig},J_A\to0\)，并且

\[
\|f_i\varphi_i+6\sqrt2\pi H_i\|_2\to0,\qquad
\left\||2\pi H_i|-\frac{q_i}{3\sqrt2}\right\|_2\to0.
\tag{1}
\]

此外

\[
s_i\to-4\quad\text{一致},\qquad
|W_i^+|\to \frac1{2\sqrt6},\qquad q_i\to\frac92
\quad\text{于 }L^2 .
\tag{2}
\]

这里 \(q_i=-s_i+\sqrt6|W_i^+|\)。

## 1. harmonic-radius patch 上真正得到什么

假设 \(x_i\) 周围存在固定尺度的 \(C^{2,\alpha}\) harmonic-radius 坐标片。缩小坐标片并拉回后，

\[
g_i\to g_\infty\quad\text{于 }C^{2,\beta}_{\rm loc},
\]

从而经 Einstein 方程 bootstrap，

\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{g_\infty}=-g_\infty,\qquad s_\infty=-4,
\tag{3}
\]

且 \(g_\infty\) 光滑。由曲率一致收敛和 (2)，

\[
|W_\infty^+|\equiv\frac1{2\sqrt6},\qquad |W_\infty^+|^2=\frac1{24}.
\tag{4}
\]

### (i) 所选 SW 二形式与本征线

调和形式 \(H_i\) 有统一全局 \(L^2\) 范数；局部椭圆估计给出子列

\[
H_i\to H_\infty
\]

于更小坐标片上光滑收敛，其中 \(H_\infty\) 调和、自对偶。由 (1)、(2) 及强局部收敛，

\[
|H_\infty|\equiv \frac{3}{4\sqrt2\pi}>0.
\tag{5}
\]

取正则化权重 \(f_i\to\sqrt{9/2}=3/\sqrt2\)，则

\[
\varphi_i\to -4\pi H_\infty,\qquad
\psi_i=\frac23\varphi_i\to
\psi_\infty=-\frac{8\pi}{3}H_\infty,
\tag{6}
\]

至少强 \(L^2_{\rm loc}\)；因此

\[
|\psi_\infty|=\sqrt2,\qquad d\psi_\infty=d^*\psi_\infty=0.
\tag{7}
\]

故在该正则片上，极限 SW 二形式处处非零、闭且自对偶，定义局部 almost-Kähler 结构，并张成一个光滑实线丛。

这里需要区分两点：

* 对**极限形式**，非消失由 harmonic-form 的局部椭圆紧性和 (1)–(2) 得到；
* 仅凭原序列的全局 \(L^2\) 估计，并不能断言每个 \(\psi_i\) 在该片上都点态非零，也不能直接获得全局 almost-Kähler 结构。那仍需要 \(C^0\) 型升级。

在当前重标度约定中 \(|\Phi_i|^2\to\sqrt2\)，不能与另一套未重标度方程中的“\(|\Phi|^2\to4\)”混用。

### (ii) \(W^+\) 的本征值重数

定义非负代数缺陷

\[
\mathcal E(W,v)=\langle Wv,v\rangle+
\sqrt{\frac23}|W|\,|v|^2.
\]

因为

\[
D_{{\rm eig},i}=2\int \mathcal E(W_i^+,\psi_i)\to0,
\]

而 \(W_i^+\to W_\infty^+\)、\(\psi_i\to\psi_\infty\neq0\)，极限上

\[
\mathcal E(W_\infty^+,\psi_\infty)=0.
\tag{8}
\]

所以 \(\psi_\infty\) 张成最低本征线，并且

\[
\lambda_{\min}
=-\sqrt{\frac23}|W_\infty^+|=-\frac16.
\tag{9}
\]

非负性本身来自迹零三维对称算子的尖锐估计

\[
\lambda_{\min}\ge-\sqrt{\frac23}|W|.
\]

取等当且仅当另外两个本征值相等。结合迹零与 (9)，

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Spec}(W_\infty^+)
=\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right)}.
\tag{10}
\]

因此答案是肯定的：**在上述正则极限片上，非负本征值缺陷加振幅和 Hodge/调和投影控制确实强制完整谱 (10)**。最低本征值简单，最大本征值重数二。

### (iii) 极限 Einstein 度量

局部极限满足

\[
\operatorname{Ric}=-g,\quad s=-4,\quad
|W^+|^2=\frac1{24},\quad
\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)=
\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right).
\tag{11}
\]

它既不是复双曲型 Kähler–Einstein bulk（后者在 \(s=-4\) 时
\(|W^+|^2=2/3\)），也不是实双曲型（后者 \(W^+=0\)）。

## 2. Derdziński 的正确后果

谱 (10) 位于

\[
\alpha=\beta=\frac1{12},\qquad \gamma=-\frac16,
\]

即**最大本征值二重、负的最低本征值简单**。因此 Catino–Dameno 关于“最大本征值一致简单”的定理不适用：这里恰为其尖锐边界

\[
\frac{\det W^+}{|W^+|^3}=-\frac1{3\sqrt6},\qquad \rho=\beta/\alpha=1.
\]

适用的是原始 Derdziński 两本征值结论：在简单最低本征线可定向的局部双覆盖上，存在正函数 \(f\)，使

\[
\widetilde g=f^2g_\infty
\]

为 Kähler 度量。其 Kähler 标量曲率 \(\widetilde s\) 为负，并由 Weyl 本征值的共形权重满足

\[
f^2\widetilde s=-1.
\tag{12}
\]

注意：不能因为 \(|W_g^+|\) 恒定，就断言这个负分支的 \(f\) 恒定。文献中常见的
\(\alpha_h^{2/3}h\) 归一化针对的是**最大简单正本征值**分支；本题处在最大本征值二重的相反分支。将该公式直接移用到这里，是导致“局部不可能”错误结论的根源。

采用几何学家的非负 Laplacian

\[
\nabla^*\nabla=d^*d=-\operatorname{div}\nabla,
\]

标量曲率共形变换与 (12)、\(s_g=-4\) 给出

\[
\boxed{\nabla^*\nabla f=\frac12 f}.
\tag{13}
\]

等价地，若 \(\Delta=\operatorname{div}\nabla\)，则

\[
\Delta f=-\frac12f.
\]

这在开集或非紧流形上完全可能有正解。因此：

\[
\boxed{\text{谱 (10) 在 }\operatorname{Ric}=-g\text{ 下并非局部不可能。}}
\]

它给出的是负标量 Kähler 度量的局部共形 Einstein 模型。

## 3. 紧致性为何产生矛盾

若同一结构存在于闭流形上，(13) 与 \(f>0\) 导致

\[
0=\int_M\nabla^*\nabla f\,d\mu
=\frac12\int_M f\,d\mu>0,
\]

矛盾。等价地，闭流形上正本征值对应的 Laplace 本征函数不可能保持正号。

这与 LeBrun–Armstrong 的全局结论一致：闭 Einstein 度量若饱和相应 monopole 不等式，则必须为 Kähler–Einstein；但 \(s=-4\) 的 Kähler 度量具有

\[
\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)
=\left(-\frac23,\frac13,\frac13\right),\qquad
|W^+|^2=\frac23,
\]

而非 (10)。所以矛盾是**紧致/全局的**，不是纯局部的。

非紧时不能无条件使用 Stokes；所需边界衰减或容量条件并未从当前局部极限推出。现有共形 Kähler–Einstein、Poincaré–Einstein 构造说明这种非紧机制本身是合理的，但供应材料尚未给出一个同时满足 (11) 全部常数条件的完整显式模型。

## 4. Bochner 公式与数值修正

Einstein 四流形上，按上述 Laplacian 约定，

\[
\frac12\Delta |W^+|^2
=
|\nabla W^+|^2+\frac{s}{2}|W^+|^2
-6\operatorname{tr}\bigl((W^+)^3\bigr).
\tag{14}
\]

对 (10)，

\[
|W^+|^2=\frac1{24},\qquad
\operatorname{tr}\bigl((W^+)^3\bigr)=-\frac1{288}.
\]

因范数恒定，(14) 给出

\[
\boxed{|\nabla W^+|^2=\frac1{16}}.
\tag{15}
\]

所以该假想局部模型的 \(W^+\) 非平行，并非局部对称。先前使用系数
\((s/3,-4)\) 得到的 \(1/24\) 不符合 Catino–Dameno 的 Einstein–Weyl Weitzenböck 方程，应改为 (14)–(15)。Bochner 公式没有产生矛盾，反而与非平行的局部共形 Kähler 模型相容。

## 5. 最强成立的定理

当前材料支持的最强结论是：

> **正则局部极限定理。**  
> 固定临界 Ishida–LeBrun 流形上的近 Einstein 序列，若在某些未缩放固定尺度 harmonic-radius 片上收敛，则任何光滑极限片都满足 (11)，其选定 SW 极限二形式是处处非零的最低 Weyl 本征形式，并局部定义 almost-Kähler 结构。该片由 Derdziński 局部共形于负标量 Kähler 度量，其共形因子满足 (13)。这些条件局部并不矛盾。

相应的全局结论仍是：

> 若另有统一全局 harmonic-radius 下界和直径上界，则得到同一闭流形上的光滑 Einstein 极限；紧致 Stokes 或 LeBrun–Armstrong 刚性随后排除该极限。因此任何假想序列必须发生 harmonic-radius 退化或直径逃逸。

不能由现有论证推出

\[
\sup_x r_h(x,g_i)\to0,
\]

因为单个正则片只产生非紧/有边界局部模型，而该模型没有局部矛盾。可推出的仍只是全局有界几何排斥，或等价的

\[
\inf_x r_h(x,g_i)\to0
\quad\text{或}\quad
\operatorname{diam}(M,g_i)\to\infty
\]

这一退化二分。

精确剩余对象是：是否存在完整非紧 Einstein 四流形满足 (11)，以及能否从原紧流形序列获得足以对其共形因子应用全局积分的衰减、有限体积或零容量条件。没有这些附加信息，Derdziński 路线不能单独排除局部正则极限。

~~~~markdown
# Step 6: 原研究交接

状态：Repair（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

本步从 Step 5 的符号分支争议出发，读取了 `workspace/notes/step5_regular_patch_and_derdzinski_boundary.tex`、Codex 的 `quantitative_deficit_analysis.md`、两份 Step 5 TTCS 集成、S0910A01 的局部刚性笔记、Cheeger–Naber 正则性原文以及现代 Derdziński 论述。随后对 Strategist 提出的投影恒等式逐指标复算，保留 δ(ω⊗ω) 的两个乘积法则项，建立了“harmonic W⁺ 加两个不同常本征值推出 ∇W⁺=0”的局部引理。Step 6 TTCS 第一项的一条可用独立分支复核了该计算、归一化和 |∇W⁺|²=1/16；另一分支不可用。第二项 TTCS 的两条分支确认了 Cheeger–Naber 正则片、有限 p 的强 W^{2,p} 传递、对角 regularized monopole 选择、非零极限调和形式和完整校准谱，但其集成仍沿用了调用前的“局部相容”判断；这一分歧随后由完整张量计算和 Derdziński 原文共同解决，而没有把重复的旧判断当作新证据。

本步读取了 S0910A01 新取得的 Derdziński 1983 原文转录，核对 Proposition 5(i) 的局部 Kähler 因子 (24|W⁺|²)^{1/3}g、Proposition 5(ii) 的本质唯一性及 Proposition 5(iii) 的常模长等价于 ∇W⁺=0。这撤回了 Step 5 笔记中关于非紧局部共形因子可能实现校准常谱的解释。相应修复已写入 `workspace/notes/step6_local_projector_obstruction_and_collapse_reduction.tex`；原 `step5_regular_patch_and_derdzinski_boundary.tex` 顶部及结尾已加明确替代说明，保留其中仍成立的弱 Bianchi 和函数空间分析。

结合固定拓扑时绝对缺陷趋零，本步把局部引理与正则片提取组合为条件清楚的新定理：固定临界 Ishida–LeBrun 流形上的假想 δ_i→0 序列必须满足 sup_p Vol B_1(p)→0，且固定正总容积迫使直径发散。变化拓扑时则只保留非塌缩点集体积比例趋零的结论。该固定/变化拓扑区别已在笔记中明确，并通过会话组消息 #230、#233 同 S0910A01、S0910A02 对齐；S0910A02 接受局部排除并指出其与正分支特殊代数曲率筛选的平行结构。

本步进一步读取 Naber–Zhang 塌缩正则性原文，记录了低维 Ricci-limit 模型、最大幂零秩、局部覆盖非塌缩、弱谐和半径、模型依赖常数和残余四维例外。研究方案保存于 `workspace/notes/step6_collapsed_unwrapping_route.md`：下一接口是 deck 平均的缺陷传输，而不是假定覆盖自动保留底空间均值。外部知识检索没有取得秩下降区域体积受 L² 曲率控制的一般定理，但带回了 covering geometry、Lott almost Ricci-flat groupoid、负 Einstein cusp 和塌缩拓扑来源。实际阅读 Lott 原文又显露出更强结构：局部阿贝尔对称下轨道体积函数满足 Δ√det G=(|F|²/4−λN)√det G；λ<0 时规则纯塌缩在闭或适当抛物基底上受到直接排除。该 near-Einstein 推广尚未构造，是后续值得并行发展的新方向。

## 当时的后续问题

沿 `workspace/notes/step6_local_projector_obstruction_and_collapse_reduction.tex` 与 `workspace/notes/step6_collapsed_unwrapping_route.md` 继续构造剩余塌缩理论，同时保持它只是完整 Yau 第26题的一条四维负分支。第一，逐段提取 Naber–Zhang Theorem 1.1、Theorem 5.1 及弱谐和半径部分的精确尺度、覆盖域、局部完备性、模型依赖和最大秩假设，区分底空间 conjugate/weak harmonic radius 与普通谐和坐标半径。以纯曲率非负密度为优先对象，重建 completion-square 与尖锐本征谱余量，使局部覆盖论证尽量不依赖把全局 SW 解本身搬到覆盖。证明或反驳一个 deck-平均传输引理：从底空间小局部均值和最大秩正常覆盖，选择固定尺度非塌缩覆盖片，使拉回缺陷均值仍趋零；明确覆盖边界、不均匀重数和 deck 轨道如何进入估计。若成立，将其与 Step 6 禁止的校准 Einstein germ 组合，排除具有统一模型尺度的最大秩规则塌缩。

第二，发展 Lott 局部阿贝尔对称 Einstein 方程的负宇宙常数版本。直接从适配度量推导 v=√det G 的方程 Δv=(|F|²/4−λN)v，并对 Ric+g 的 L∞ 缺陷计算定量误差项。研究在长而处处塌缩的闭四流形上，如何用 cutoff、容量、轨道体积有界性或 groupoid 极限积分该方程；确定 λ=−1 的正零阶项是否排除所有规则纯阿贝尔区域，或迫使可测边界通量集中在秩下降、奇异纤维和曲率集中集合。把这一结构与 Naber–Zhang 的最大秩/秩下降分解、Lott 的 Riemannian groupoid 描述及 S0910A02 的圆纤维计算比较，寻找比单一 S¹ 模型更一般的机制。

第三，若规则区域被排除或其体积趋零，量化剩余奇异区域必须承载什么：Euler 与 signature 的 Chern–Weil 能量、全部 monopole harmonic classes、W⁻ 集中或残余四维 Ricci-flat bubbles。现有检索未提供秩下降区域的体积定理，因此可尝试从四维 L² 曲率预算、局部拓扑、fibered fundamental group 秩跳变及覆盖 multiplicity 自行建立关系；同时用 K3 奇异纤维、hyperbolic cusp、product-hyperbolic collapse 和 Eguchi–Hanson residual factor 检验每一步，避免把规则模型结论扩大到奇异塌缩。

在推进上述构造时，持续区分固定 A 的绝对误差与 A_i→∞ 的归一化误差，并独立核对是否有处处单位尺度塌缩、固定总容积、Ric≈−g 的真实模型。把任何新排除定理明确限定于其几何假设。与 S0910A02 保持交流，因为正分支的局部覆盖与奇异 strata 问题共享工具，但不要把两种 Einstein 常数下轨道体积方程的符号混同。若该塌缩线不能触及秩下降主体，应回到更广路线比较，而不是把临界 LeBrun 家族当作完整原题。研究继续处于 Explore，不进入最终表达或 Lean 包装。
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 6: collapsed unwrapping route after the local calibrated-germ exclusion

## Mathematical starting point

The corrected local theorem is in `step6_local_projector_obstruction_and_collapse_reduction.tex`: a smooth Einstein four-dimensional germ with

\[
\operatorname{Ric}=-g,\qquad
\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)=(-1/6,1/12,1/12)
\]

cannot exist. The full projector divergence equation forces the simple self-dual eigenform parallel, while the Einstein--Weyl equation requires \(|\nabla W^+|^2=1/16\). Hence, on a fixed exact-boundary Ishida--LeBrun manifold, any hypothetical sequence with \(\|\operatorname{Ric}+g\|_{L^\infty}\to0\) must satisfy

\[
\sup_p\operatorname{Vol}B_1(p)\to0.
\]

For varying topology, only a vanishing *volume fraction* of noncollapsed unit balls is presently established because the curvature/SW errors are normalized by \(A_i\).

## What Naber--Zhang actually contributes

The relevant source is

`Knowledge/objects/papers/Topology-and-ε-regularity-theorems-on-collapsed-manifolds-with-Ricci-cu--4c64d7206fcd--56043259b64c/object.md`.

Their Theorem 1.1 assumes a two-sided Ricci bound, local relative compactness, Gromov--Hausdorff closeness

\[
B_2(p)\simeq B_2(0^{k-\ell},z^\ell)\subset\mathbb R^{k-\ell}\times Z^\ell,
\qquad \ell\le3,
\]

and maximal nilpotency rank

\[
\operatorname{rank}\Gamma_\delta(p)=n-k,
\qquad
\Gamma_\delta(p)=\operatorname{Image}[\pi_1(B_\delta(p))\to\pi_1(B_2(p))].
\]

It then supplies a lower conjugate/weak harmonic radius bound; for exact Einstein inputs it upgrades to curvature control, while for merely bounded Ricci the harmonic-radius conclusion is the relevant one. Its proof also gives noncollapse on a local universal cover. The residual-dimension restriction \(\ell\le3\) is sharp; a four-dimensional Eguchi--Hanson factor defeats the conclusion. Constants depend on the lower-dimensional Ricci-limit model through a noncollapsing radius.

This does not automatically settle the collapsed LeBrun sequence. The following must all be supplied at the same collapsed ball:

1. a controlled lower-dimensional GH model;
2. maximal fibered nilpotency rank;
3. a cover ball of fixed geometric size with a harmonic chart;
4. preservation of the small *mean* calibrated deficit after lifting.

The last point was resolved in Step 8 for normal covers of buffered domains whose relevant cover balls remain interior: disjoint deck translates and Bishop--Gromov comparison give a sheet-independent bound of the cover-ball mean by the corresponding base-ball mean. See `step8_cover_mean_transport_and_model_scope_corrections.md`. The remaining issue is obtaining fixed-scale Naber--Zhang cover regularity on a positive-volume set, not deck multiplicity itself.

## A precise conditional extension

Let \(F_i\ge0\) collect the completion-square and sharp spectral defects whose zero set yields the calibrated spectrum. Suppose a sequence of collapsed balls \(B_2(p_i)\) has:

- bounded Ricci and the Naber--Zhang GH/rank hypotheses with uniform model constants;
- normal covers \(\pi_i:\widehat B_2(p_i)\to B_2(p_i)\) containing fixed-size noncollapsed harmonic charts \(U_i\);
- a transport estimate
  \[
  \fint_{U_i}\pi_i^*F_i\to0.
  \]

Then the same harmonic-coordinate \(W^{2,p}\) passage used in the noncollapsed case gives a smooth Einstein germ with the forbidden calibrated spectrum. Therefore no positive-volume family of collapsed balls can satisfy all three properties simultaneously.

This conditional statement turns the remaining geometry into two alternatives:

- **uniformly modeled maximal-rank collapse:** complete local universal covers expose a forbidden calibrated germ; Step 8's mean-transfer lemma closes the multiplicity issue;
- **inaccessible collapse:** on almost all relevant volume, at least one of GH model control, maximal rank, or uniform model scale fails, or unwrapping exists only at radii tending to zero. The failure can be associated with rank drop, singular fibers, residual four-dimensional bubbles, or concentration regions.

The K3 example in Naber--Zhang is structurally instructive: regular torus fibers have maximal rank, while singular Kodaira fibers have rank drop and curvature concentration. For Yau 26 this suggests locating the Euler/signature and monopole topology specifically on the rank-drop/concentration set, rather than trying to forbid collapse abstractly.

## Relation to the positive branch

S0910A02's constant-length principal-circle calculation excludes one regular free-circle model under tight positive pinching, while \(\chi=0\) excludes a global free circle action on the relevant positive four-manifolds. Those results do not cover warped fibers or singular strata. The shared mechanism is now clear: both signs require distinguishing collapse that unwraps to controlled smooth geometry from collapse whose singular/rank-drop regions carry the essential topology. The negative critical route has the additional forbidden calibrated germ, which provides a sharp target once a cover chart and deficit transport are available.

## Next high-value work

1. Prove a volume-distribution theorem for points satisfying the uniform Naber--Zhang hypotheses: fixed-scale low-dimensional GH model, maximal fibered nilpotency rank, and model noncollapsing radius bounded below.
2. Quantify the complementary regions: rank drop, degeneration of the lower-dimensional model scale, residual four-dimensional cores, and unwrapping only at radii tending to zero.
3. Relate those failures to Euler/signature and monopole curvature budgets without invoking an Einstein-only curvature decomposition.
4. Keep varying-topology and fixed-topology error scales separate. Absolute deficit vanishing is available only for fixed \(A\); normalized smallness does not exclude isolated noncollapsed/concentrated islands.

This remains a four-dimensional negative-branch reduction, not a solution of either normalized branch in all dimensions.
~~~~

~~~~latex
% Step 6: constant-spectrum projector obstruction and the corrected collapse reduction
% This note supersedes the "local compatibility" section of
% step5_regular_patch_and_derdzinski_boundary.tex.

\section{Setting}
Let $M$ be a fixed critical Ishida--LeBrun four-manifold,
\[
 D=A/3,
 \qquad
 \delta_i=\|g_i^{-1}(\Ric_{g_i}+g_i)\|_{L^\infty}\to0.
\]
The genuine scalar--Weyl estimate, the exact nonnegative deficit decomposition,
and Chern--Weil give absolute errors $O(A\delta_i^2)$ because $A$ is fixed.  In
particular,
\[
 \int_M(s_i+8\sqrt6|W_i^+|)^2\to0,
\]
and a selected sign monopole class has harmonic representative and eigenvalue
defects tending to zero.  The issue reviewed here is what happens if a unit ball
is noncollapsed.

\section{A constant-spectrum harmonic-Weyl lemma}
\textbf{Lemma.}  Let $(U^4,g)$ be oriented.  Suppose $\delta W^+=0$ and, as an
endomorphism of $\Lambda^+$, $W^+$ has two distinct constant eigenvalues: a
simple eigenvalue $\lambda$ and a double eigenvalue $\mu$.  Then $\nabla W^+=0$.

Choose locally an eigenform $\omega$ of constant norm spanning the simple
line.  With the convention $\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\tfrac12
\alpha_{ab}\beta^{ab}$ and $|\omega|^2=2$, the orthogonal projection onto
$\mathbb R\omega$ is represented, up to the harmless tensor-action convention,
by a nonzero constant multiple of $\omega\otimes\omega$.  Thus
\[
 W^+=\mu I_{\Lambda^+}+(\lambda-\mu)P_\omega.
\]
Since the eigenvalues and $I_{\Lambda^+}$ are parallel, $\delta W^+=0$ gives
\[
 (\nabla^a\omega_{ab})\omega_{cd}
   +\omega_{ab}\nabla^a\omega_{cd}=0.                 \tag{1}
\]
The first term in (1) must not be omitted.  Contracting (1) with
$\omega^{cd}$ and using constant length yields
\[
 \nabla^a\omega_{ab}=0.                                \tag{2}
\]
Substitution into (1) gives
\[
 \omega_{ab}\nabla^a\omega_{cd}=0.                    \tag{3}
\]
A nonzero self-dual two-form in dimension four is nondegenerate; after the
normalization above, $\omega_a{}^c\omega_c{}^b=-\delta_a{}^b$.  Hence (3)
forces $\nabla\omega=0$, so $\nabla P_\omega=0$ and $\nabla W^+=0$.  This
argument depends only on $\lambda\ne\mu$, not on their signs.

This direct computation agrees with Derdzi\'nski's 1983 Proposition 5: when
$\delta W^+=0$ and $W^+$ has at most two eigenvalues, the conformal metric
\[
 \bar g=(24|W^+|^2)^{1/3}g
\]
is locally K\"ahler on $\{W^+\ne0\}$, and Proposition 5(iii) states that
$|W^+|^2$ is constant exactly when $\nabla W^+=0$.  The primary text is at
\texttt{Sessions/S0910A01/workspace/notes/sources/derdzinski\_1983\_self\_dual\_kahler\_einstein\_four.txt}, lines 1024--1077.  Thus the Step 5 suggestion that an arbitrary nonconstant positive solution of a scalar conformal equation could realize the calibrated constant spectrum was incomplete: K\"ahler closure fixes the conformal factor.

\section{Exclusion of the calibrated Einstein germ}
For an Einstein four-metric the endomorphism Weitzenb\"ock equation is
\[
 0=\nabla^*\nabla W^+ +\frac{s}{2}W^+-6(W^+)^2
       +2|W^+|^2 I.
\]
At
\[
 s=-4,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Spec}(W^+)=\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right),
\]
one has $|W^+|^2=1/24$ and $\det W^+=-1/864$.  The scalar identity
\[
 \Delta|W^+|^2=2|\nabla W^+|^2+s|W^+|^2-36\det W^+
\]
therefore requires
\[
 |\nabla W^+|^2=\frac1{16}.                             \tag{4}
\]
The lemma instead gives $\nabla W^+=0$.  Hence no smooth open Einstein four-manifold can carry this constant calibrated spectrum.  Equivalently, the parallel simple eigenform makes $g$ locally K\"ahler, whereas a K\"ahler metric with $s=-4$ has self-dual Weyl spectrum
$(-2/3,1/3,1/3)$ in this orientation.

\section{Regular-patch transfer on a fixed boundary manifold}
Suppose for a subsequence there are points $p_i$ with
\[
 \Vol_{g_i}B_1(p_i)\ge v>0.                              \tag{5}
\]
For large $i$, $|\Ric_{g_i}|\le3$.  Cheeger--Naber Theorem 1.13 gives
\[
 \Vol\!\left(T_r\{x\in B_1(p_i):r_h(x)\le r\}\right)
 \le C(v)r^4.                                             \tag{6}
\]
Bishop--Gromov supplies a lower bound for $\Vol B_{1/2}(p_i)$.  Taking a
fixed small $\rho(v)$ in (6) selects $x_i\in B_{1/2}(p_i)$ with a fixed
harmonic coordinate radius.  On a smaller common chart,
\[
 g_i\to g_\infty\quad\hbox{strongly in }C^{1,\beta}_{\rm loc},
 \qquad g_i\rightharpoonup g_\infty\quad\hbox{in }W^{2,p}_{\rm loc}.
\]
The harmonic-coordinate Ricci equation and
$\Ric(g_i)+g_i\to0$ in $L^\infty$ imply weakly that
$\Ric(g_\infty)=-g_\infty$; the limit bootstraps to smooth.  Interior
$W^{2,p}$ estimates for the difference equation then give strong
$W^{2,p}_{\rm loc}$ convergence for finite $p$.  No $C^{2,\alpha}$ control of
the approximating metrics is asserted.

Because all relevant total defects are nonnegative and converge absolutely to
zero for fixed $A$, their restrictions to this chart converge to zero.  The
completion square gives
\[
 s_\infty=-4,
 \qquad |W_\infty^+|=\frac1{2\sqrt6}.                    \tag{7}
\]
Choose the regularized rescaled monopoles diagonally so their smoothing error
is $o(\delta_i^2)$.  The fixed selected sign class has harmonic self-dual
representatives $H_i$.  Local elliptic compactness and the amplitude/projection
defects give a smooth limit
\[
 |H_\infty|=\frac{3}{4\sqrt2\pi}>0.                      \tag{8}
\]
The SW maximum estimate supplies local uniform integrability for the quadratic
forms.  Strong curvature convergence and the nonnegative eigenvalue defect then
put $H_\infty$ in the sharp lowest eigenline.  The trace-free $3\times3$
equality case yields
\[
 \operatorname{Spec}(W_\infty^+)
 =\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right).           \tag{9}
\]
Equations (7)--(9) contradict the preceding local lemma.  Therefore, for a
\emph{fixed} critical boundary manifold,
\[
 \boxed{\sup_{p\in M}\Vol_{g_i}B_1(p)\longrightarrow0.}  \tag{10}
\]
Indeed, failure of (10) gives (5) immediately; no volume-random selection is
needed because the fixed-$A$ deficits vanish absolutely on every subset.

If topology varies with $A_i\to\infty$, the available errors are generally only
$o(A_i)$, not absolute $o(1)$.  A small noncollapsed island may then absorb a
nonvanishing amount of defect.  The corresponding rigorously supported result
is measure-relative: for every fixed $v>0$, the volume fraction of
$\{p:\Vol B_1(p)\ge v\}$ tends to zero, using local-mean averaging before
applying (6).  One must not replace this varying-topology statement by (10).

\section{What this changes and what remains}
The local calibrated Einstein model is inconsistent, so complete finite-volume
searches for that exact model are no longer useful.  A hypothetical fixed
critical sequence must collapse at unit scale everywhere while retaining total
volume $\Vol(g_i)\to32\pi^2A/9$; consequently its diameter must diverge.  The
remaining geometry can hide only through collapsed local quotients/covers,
long thin regions, singular-fiber strata, or curvature/topology concentration.
The next valuable question is whether typical collapsed balls can be locally
unwrapped to noncollapsed harmonic charts while preserving small pulled-back
LeBrun deficit.  Maximal-rank Naber--Zhang collapse, constant-fibre-length
circle models, and singular/fixed strata should be separated rather than
conflated.  A controlled unwrapping theorem would reproduce the local
contradiction on the cover; failure of such unwrapping would identify precisely
where topology or curvature must concentrate.

This is a sharp reduction for one four-dimensional negative branch.  It neither
settles the positive normalized branch nor the statement in all dimensions,
and hence does not by itself prove or refute Yau's Problem 26.
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 7: 原研究交接

状态：Verify（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

本步从 Step 6 的塌缩归约出发，发展了完整的轨道体积排除机制。首先阅读 Lott (1708.06780) 的自由阿贝尔 Einstein 适配度量轨道体积方程 Δv = (|F|²/4 - λN)v，在 λ = -1 下识别出严格正系数 |F|²/4 + N ≥ 1，使 v 严格次调和。对抛物基底（dim ≥ 2 紧空间补有限点）和圆周基底分别建立了排除论证，并推导近 Einstein 版本（系数 N(1-δ)）。代数验证脚本 verify_orbit_volume_negative_einstein.py 通过。

随后用 TTCS 双任务组研究 nil³ 情形。Generator 独立推导出精确方程 v'' = (3 - ρ/2)v（ρ = a₃²/(a₁²a₂²)），系数因负 Heisenberg 纤维标量曲率而低于阿贝尔值 3。关键的 ρ 极大值原理给出圆周上 ρ ≤ 2/3，确保 v'' ≥ (8/3)v > 0 排除圆周。CH² horospherical cusp（ρ = 2/3, μ = 1/3）被确认为射线上的真实解。Verifier 同时核对了阿贝尔排除的正确性，发现并否定了先前笔记中的容量估计（c∫η² ≤ ∫|∇η|² 为假）、指出 v 的 L∞ 有界性需额外论证，以及 Cheeger-Tian 框架对近 Einstein 度量的适用性尚有缺口。

收到 A01 msg #238 后，独立写脚本 verify_nil3_sign_check.py 用 CH² 模型精确验证：v''/v = 8/3 = 3 - 1/3，否定 A01 的 v'' = (3+μ)v。通过 msg #239 发送了详细修正。A01 的圆周排除因极大值原理仍成立，但其普遍不等式和'nil³ 更难'的断言均为假。

最终笔记 step7_orbit_volume_negative_einstein_collapse.tex 已更新：加入纠正后的 nil³ 分析节，撤回错误容量估计，修改汇总表。step7_consolidated_status.md 给出了完整的当前状态。与 A02 交叉：其正分支 Weyl 预算、det R₊ 修正和 Pohozaev 桥梁思路（msg #237）与本步负分支轨道体积分析互补但独立。

## 当时的后续问题

三项关键核验需求：

第一，核定 nil³ 轨道体积方程的正确符号和完整推导链。TTCS 与 A03 的 CH² 验证一致给出 v'' = (3-μ)v，而 A01 声称 (3+μ)v。需要从 Milnor 纤维 Ricci 特征值（r₁=r₂=-μ, r₃=+μ）出发，逐行验证超曲面 Ricci 公式、Einstein 分量 E1(+μ)、E3(-μ) 的符号、求和得到 2Σfᵢfⱼ = 2-μ，以及 v''/v = 3-μ。验证圆周极大值原理 ρ ≤ 2/3 和闭区间两端 v→0 的凸性排除。确认 CH² cusp 在射线上存在但不能闭合为圆周。判断 A01 Step 9 的'Complete regular-collapse exclusion'定理和'Fixed-topology negative pinching obstruction'是否因符号错误而需要修正，以及修正后是否仍可救回。

第二，评估 TTCS 核验指出的三个缺口：(a) 容量估计已确认为假（反例清楚），需确认后续论证不依赖它；(b) v 的 L∞ 有界性：从什么条件能得到轨道体积的全局上界？Lott 原文在定理假设中包含'det G bounded above'，这对塌缩序列是否自动成立？(c) Cheeger-Tian 框架对 |Ric+g| ≤ δ（非精确 Einstein）的适用性：是否有已知定理（Li 2010, 或 CFG 的有界截面曲率条件）给出所需的正则区域？这三个缺口中哪些是可以封闭的，哪些构成真正的逻辑断裂？

第三，从全局视角评估四维负分支的战略位置。现在阿贝尔和 nil³ 圆周/闭区间塌缩都被排除，仅剩 cusp 段和爆破区域。原题要求固定维数对两个符号分支都给出证明或反例。当前证据是否足以在某个受限但有价值的范围内给出严格定理（如'固定拓扑的临界 Ishida-LeBrun 族的负分支 gap'），还是因上述缺口导致任何正式定理都不成立？评估整个轨道体积路线是否是四维负分支最有价值的推进方向，以及与正分支和高维的关系。
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 7 results after Step 8 review

The Step 7 computations supplied useful exact-model identities, but they do not classify an arbitrary collapsed near-Einstein sequence. The current bridge and all scope corrections are in:

`step8_cover_mean_transport_and_model_scope_corrections.md`.

## Exact model results retained

### Abelian adapted metrics

For an exact free isometric abelian adapted metric,

\[
\Delta_B\sqrt{\det G}=\left(|F|^2/4-\lambda N\right)\sqrt{\det G}.
\]

For \(\lambda<0\), this excludes the model when the base is parabolic and the orbit-volume function is bounded above. A circle base is excluded by periodic integration. Finite total volume does not imply bounded orbit volume, polar ends, or parabolicity. The near-Einstein coefficient \(N(1-\delta)\) is available only when the action is exactly isometric and adapted to the actual metric.

### Exact \(\mathrm{nil}^3\) cohomogeneity-one metrics

With \([E_1,E_2]=\sqrt\rho E_3\),

\[
v''=(3-\rho/2)v.
\]

This sign is verified by the \(\mathbb{CH}^2\) cusp. On a circle, the full Einstein trace system gives \(\rho\le2/3\), hence \(v''\ge(8/3)v\), contradicting periodicity.

On a finite interval, convexity follows only if endpoint behavior controls \(\rho\), e.g. \(\limsup_{\partial I}\rho<6\). With that condition and \(v\to0\) at both finite endpoints, a positive solution is impossible. Without endpoint control, \(\rho\) may diverge and no global convexity follows.

The \(\mathbb{CH}^2\) nil cusp has finite volume and infinite base length:

\[
v(s)=Ce^{4s/\sqrt6},\qquad s\in(-\infty,0].
\]

Thus finite volume gives no cusp-length bound.

## Errors withdrawn

- The cover degree cannot be dropped from a lifted total integral.
- Absolute smallness of the global deficit does not itself give a small lifted integral.
- The proposed capacity inequality is false and gives no regular-region volume estimate.
- Exact abelian and \(\mathrm{nil}^3\) models do not exhaust collapse of the actual pinched metrics.
- Interval \(\mathrm{nil}^3\) collapse is not excluded without endpoint control of \(\rho\).
- A fixed-topology negative pinching gap has not been proved.

## New bridge established in Step 8

For a normal local cover of a buffered base domain whose radius-\(3r\) cover ball remains interior, and with \(\operatorname{Ric}\ge-(n-1)Kg\), a cover-ball mean is controlled by the corresponding base-ball mean:

\[
\fint_{B_r(\hat p)}\pi^*F
\le \frac{V_{-K}^{(n)}(3r)}{V_{-K}^{(n)}(r)}
\fint_{B_r(p)}F.
\]

Combined with Fubini/Bishop–Gromov point selection and Naber–Zhang Proposition 6.4, this excludes any positive-volume set of collapsed points that has, at a fixed scale, a uniformly controlled low-dimensional model, maximal fibered nilpotency rank, and nondegenerating model scale. The unresolved object is the volume distribution of such Naber–Zhang-good points versus rank-drop, model-degenerate, residual-four-dimensional, and shrinking-scale regions.
~~~~

~~~~latex
% Step 7 historical note: exact orbit-volume model calculations
% S0910A03 Agent2 (Constructor) — Explore
%
% CORRECTED IN STEP 8. The exact identities below remain useful only under
% their stated symmetry and base hypotheses. The total-deficit transport,
% capacity, exhaustive-collapse, unconditional interval nil^3, and bounded
% cusp-length statements are superseded by
% step8_cover_mean_transport_and_model_scope_corrections.md.
% No fixed-topology pinching gap follows from this note.
%
% Sources: Lott (arxiv:1708.06780) eq. (2.9), Prop. 2.10;
%   Cheeger--Naber (Ann. Math. 2015); Naber--Zhang (Geom. Topol. 2016).

\section{The orbit-volume equation for negative Einstein metrics}

Let $M^{n+N}$ carry an adapted metric with free local isometric
$\mathbb R^N$-action:
\[
 \bar g=\sum_{I,J}G_{IJ}(dx^I+A^I)(dx^J+A^J)+g_B,
\]
where $G_{IJ}$ is a positive-definite symmetric matrix on the base $B^n$,
$A^I$ are connection one-forms, and $g_B$ is a Riemannian metric on $B$.
Put $v=\sqrt{\det G}$ (the orbit-volume function) and
$|F|^2=g^{\alpha\gamma}g^{\beta\delta}G_{IJ}F_{\alpha\beta}^I F_{\gamma\delta}^J$.

\textbf{Lott's equation} \cite[eq.\ (2.9)]{Lott2020}:
if $\operatorname{Ric}(\bar g)=\lambda\bar g$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lott}
 \Delta_B v=\Bigl(\frac{|F|^2}{4}-\lambda N\Bigr)v.
\end{equation}
(The Laplacian is the geometer's $\Delta=\operatorname{tr}\nabla^2$, so
$\Delta v\ge0$ means $v$ is subharmonic.)

For the \textbf{negative normalized branch} $\lambda=-1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:negein}
 \Delta_B v=\Bigl(\frac{|F|^2}{4}+N\Bigr)v.
\end{equation}
Since $|F|^2\ge0$ and $N\ge1$, the coefficient is
$\ge N\ge1>0$.  Therefore:
\begin{quote}
\emph{Wherever $v>0$, the orbit-volume function $v$ is strictly
subharmonic.}
\end{quote}

This is qualitatively different from the Ricci-flat case $\lambda=0$,
where $\Delta v=(|F|^2/4)v\ge0$ merely forces $v$ constant and $F=0$
on parabolic bases, permitting nontrivial semiflat K\"ahler collapse
(K3 examples exist).

\section{Exclusion of free abelian negative Einstein collapse}

\textbf{Proposition.}  Let $(B^n,g_B)$ be a connected Riemannian manifold
(or orbifold), and let $\mathcal X$ be a Riemannian groupoid over $B$
with free abelian $\mathbb R^N$ symmetry ($N\ge1$) and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{\mathcal X}=\lambda g_{\mathcal X}$ with $\lambda<0$.
If $B$ is parabolic and $\det G$ is bounded above, then the free abelian
structure is impossible: no such $\mathcal X$ exists.

\textit{Proof.}
From \eqref{eq:negein}, $v=\sqrt{\det G}\ge0$ satisfies
$\Delta v\ge(-\lambda N)v$ with $-\lambda N>0$.
On the open set $\{v>0\}$, $v$ is strictly subharmonic.
Since $v\ge0$ everywhere and $\det G$ bounded above implies $v$ bounded
above, on a parabolic base a bounded-above subharmonic function is
constant (see \cite[Thm.\ 5.1]{Grigoryan1999}).
If $v=c>0$ is constant, then $\Delta v=0$ but the right side
$(-\lambda N)c>0$: contradiction.
If $v\equiv0$, then $\det G\equiv0$, contradicting the free abelian
structure (which requires positive-definite $G$). \qed

\subsection*{Scope in four dimensions}
For an exact adapted model, the proposition applies in any orbit dimension
provided its hypotheses are independently verified.  In base dimensions two
or three, a punctured compact smooth/orbifold base with polar punctures is a
standard parabolic case, but finite total four-volume does \emph{not} imply
that $v$ is bounded.  Thus no general free-circle or free-$T^2$ collapse
exclusion follows from volume alone.  For a circle base, periodic integration
excludes the exact abelian model.  For an interval, endpoint behavior must be
specified.  If the abelian action is transitive ($N=4$), the adapted metric is
left-invariant on an abelian group and hence flat, so it cannot satisfy
$\operatorname{Ric}=-g$.
\section{The quantitative near-Einstein identity under an exact adapted action}

Suppose the actual metric $g_i$ itself carries an exact local free isometric
$\mathbb R^N$-action and adapted decomposition.  This is an additional model
hypothesis; it is not supplied by the pinching assumption or by an unverified
Cheeger--Tian regular region.
If the region carries a local free $\mathbb R^N$-action adapted to $g_i$,
the vertical trace of $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_i}=-g_i+E_i$ gives
\[
 N\lambda_i+\operatorname{tr}_{\rm vert}E_i
 =-\frac12 g^{\alpha\beta}G^{IJ}G_{IJ;\alpha\beta}+\cdots+\frac{|F|^2}{4}
\]
with $\lambda_i=-1$ and $|\operatorname{tr}_{\rm vert}E_i|\le N\delta_i$.
Hence the near-Einstein orbit-volume inequality is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nearein}
 \Delta_B v\ge\Bigl(\frac{|F|^2}{4}+N(1-\delta_i)\Bigr)v
 \ge N(1-\delta_i)\,v.
\end{equation}
For $\delta_i<1$, the coefficient $c_i=N(1-\delta_i)>0$.

\subsection*{Capacity estimate (RETRACTED)}
\emph{The capacity estimate ``$c\int\eta^2\le\int|\nabla\eta|^2$''
claimed in an earlier draft is false.  The IPP/AM--GM derivation has
a sign error: the squared term in the expansion has the wrong direction
to absorb the cross term.  Counterexample: $v=e^{\sqrt c\,x}$ on
$\mathbb R$ satisfies $v''=cv$ but $c\int\eta_R^2\asymp R$ while
$\int|\eta_R'|^2=O(1)$.  Only those parabolic or periodic arguments whose
separate global hypotheses are verified remain valid.}

\section{Weighted volume and corrected mean transport}

This historical calculation motivates the issue; the rigorous normal-cover
mean lemma and its hypotheses are in the Step~8 correction.

\subsection*{Volume pushdown}
On a regular abelian region, the total-space volume element pushes down
to the base as
\[
 d\mu_M=v\cdot(\text{lattice factors})\cdot d\mu_B.
\]
If $\mathcal F$ is a nonneg pointwise scalar on $M$ (e.g., a Ricci
or curvature defect), its integral over a tube $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is
\[
 \int_{\pi^{-1}(U)}\mathcal F\,d\mu_M
 =\int_U\Bigl(\int_{\text{fiber}}\mathcal F\Bigr)\,v\,d\mu_B
 =\int_U\overline{\mathcal F}\cdot v\,d\mu_B,
\]
where $\overline{\mathcal F}$ denotes the fiberwise average.

\subsection*{Deficit amplification under unwrapping}
When the torus fiber of length $\sim v^{1/N}$ is unwrapped by a local
normal cover $\hat\pi:\hat M\to M$, the covering degree is $\sim1/v$
(in appropriate units).  A noncollapsed ball $\hat B$ on the cover
satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Vol}(\hat B)\sim1
 \quad(\text{noncollapsed}).
\]
The pullback of $\mathcal F$ satisfies
\[
 \fint_{\hat B}\hat\pi^*\mathcal F
 \sim\frac{1}{v}\cdot\fint_{B}\mathcal F\cdot v\,d\mu_B.
\]
Thus \textbf{small $v$ amplifies pointwise defects on the cover}, as the
Strategist noted: a region with tiny fiber volume may carry little
base-space error ($\overline{\mathcal F}\cdot v$ small) yet substantial
error on the noncollapsed cover chart ($\overline{\mathcal F}$ itself
large).

\subsection*{Correct object: a local mean}
The covering-degree identity does \emph{not} imply that the cover integral is
bounded by the total downstairs deficit: the degree may diverge.  For complete
finite covers, numerator and volume both multiply, preserving the mean; for
cover balls, multiplicity is nonconstant.  Step~8 proves a normal-cover
mean-transfer lemma using disjoint deck translates and Bishop--Gromov
comparison.  Absolute global integral smallness alone is insufficient.

\subsection*{No capacity consequence}
The retracted capacity inequality gives no volume or boundary-cost estimate.
Subharmonicity retains only the conditional Liouville statement for an exact
adapted action over a parabolic base with bounded $v$.  It does not classify
the collapsed regime or force the surviving geometry to be cusp-like.

\section{Why these model identities do not yet apply to the pinched sequence}

Fixing a critical Ishida--LeBrun manifold gives absolute calibrated deficit
convergence and, by Step~6, everywhere unit-scale collapse for a hypothetical
sequence.  It does \emph{not} give the Einstein-only Cheeger--Tian curvature
decomposition asserted in an earlier draft: an $L^\infty$ bound on
$\operatorname{Ric}+g$ does not control its derivatives and therefore does not
produce bounded-curvature CFG regions or a smooth Einstein groupoid by that
route.

Even if an exact adapted abelian limit model were available, the parabolic
argument would still require a genuinely parabolic base with polar ends and a
bounded orbit-volume function; finite total volume supplies only an $L^1$
condition.  Hence the exact abelian model theorem cannot be counted as an
exclusion of the actual collapsed sequence.

The valid replacement is the Step~8 cover-mean theorem.  At points satisfying
uniform Naber--Zhang low-dimensional GH control, maximal fibered nilpotency
rank, and a nondegenerating model scale, the local universal cover has fixed
harmonic radius.  A sheet-independent mean-transfer inequality then carries a
small base-ball calibrated mean to the cover chart, where the forbidden local
Einstein spectrum gives a contradiction.  What remains open is the volume
occupied by points failing these uniform Naber--Zhang hypotheses.

\section{The nil$^3$ case: corrected analysis}

For 4D collapse with $\operatorname{nil}^3$ (Heisenberg) local symmetry,
the base is 1-dimensional and the fiber is a nilmanifold with
$[e_1,e_2]=e_3$.  From the hypersurface Ricci formula
and the Milnor fiber eigenvalues $r_1=r_2=-\mu$, $r_3=+\mu$
where $\mu=a_3^2/(2a_1^2a_2^2)$, the orbit-volume equation becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nil3}
 v''=\Bigl(3-\mu\Bigr)v
 =\Bigl(3-\frac{a_3^2}{2a_1^2a_2^2}\Bigr)v.
\end{equation}
The Heisenberg structure constant \textbf{reduces} the coefficient from~3,
because the fiber scalar curvature $-\mu$ is negative.  The competing
$3+\mu$ formula in an earlier peer message had swapped the horizontal and
central fiber-Ricci signs; the peer has since retracted it.  The
$\mathbb{CH}^2$ cusp and \texttt{verify\_nil3\_sign\_check.py} independently
verify the displayed sign.

\subsection*{Circle base exclusion via maximum principle}
The full Einstein ODE system includes
$\rho'=2\rho D$ where $D=f_3-f_1-f_2$ and $\rho=2\mu$.
At an interior maximum of $\rho$, $D=0$ and
$\rho''=2\rho D'=\rho(3\rho-2)$.  Since $\rho''\le0$ at a maximum,
$\rho\le2/3$.  On a circle, $\rho$ attains its maximum in the interior,
so $\rho\le2/3$ everywhere, hence $\mu\le1/3$ and
\[
 v''\ge\frac83v>0.
\]
Integrating: $0=\int v''\ge\frac83\int v>0$, contradiction.

\subsection*{Interval base: cusps exist}
On a half-line, the standard $\mathbb{CH}^2$ horospherical metric
\[
 g=ds^2+e^{2s/\sqrt6}(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)
   +\tfrac23e^{4s/\sqrt6}\theta_3^2,
 \qquad\mu=\tfrac13,
\]
satisfies $\operatorname{Ric}=-g$ with $v\sim e^{4s/\sqrt6}$.
Taking a lattice quotient in the Heisenberg fiber gives a finite-volume
nil cusp.  This is a genuine negative Einstein solution with
$\text{nil}^3$ structure.  A two-ended finite interval is excluded by
convexity only when the endpoint behavior controls $\rho=2\mu$ (for example
$\limsup_{\partial I}\rho<6$) and $v\to0$ at both finite-distance endpoints.
If $\rho$ diverges at an endpoint, the interior maximum argument gives no
global convexity estimate.  A cusp can have infinite base length and finite
volume; see the Step~8 correction.

\subsection*{Unresolved singular and inaccessible regimes}
The model equations do not control rank-drop strata, singular fibers,
residual four-dimensional cores, curvature concentration, or regions whose
local covers become regular only at scales tending to zero.  Chern--Gauss--Bonnet
gives a fixed total $L^2$ curvature budget on fixed topology, but bounded Ricci
alone does not decompose the manifold into finitely many blowup balls and a
bounded-curvature complement.  The supported Step~8 statement instead excludes
positive-volume families of points satisfying uniform Naber--Zhang cover
hypotheses.  Determining the volume occupied by the complementary failure modes
is open.

\subsection*{Updated summary of the four-dimensional negative critical route}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\textbf{Regime} & \textbf{Status} \\
\hline
Noncollapsed regular patches & Excluded (Step~6 local spectral contradiction) \\
Exact abelian model, parabolic base & Excluded if $v$ bounded and action adapted \\
Exact abelian model, circle base & Excluded by periodic integration \\
Exact abelian model, interval base & Requires endpoint data \\
Exact $\text{nil}^3$ model, circle base & Excluded ($\rho\le2/3$, $v''\ge\frac83v$) \\
Exact $\text{nil}^3$ model, finite interval & Excluded only with endpoint $\limsup\rho<6$ and $v\to0$ \\
$\mathbb{CH}^2$ nil cusp & Exists; finite volume and infinite base length \\
Actual collapsed near-Einstein sequence & Open; exact models do not exhaust it \\
Positive branch, all dimensions & Open (separate mechanisms) \\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

These are exact-model statements relevant to the four-dimensional negative
branch.  They do not classify a fixed critical Ishida--LeBrun near-Einstein
sequence and do not establish a pinching gap.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Key files:}
\texttt{step6\_local\_projector\_obstruction\_and\_collapse\_reduction.tex}
(local spectral exclusion),
\texttt{step6\_collapsed\_unwrapping\_route.md}
(collapse route plan),
\texttt{scripts/verify\_orbit\_volume\_negative\_einstein.py}
(algebraic verification).
This note:
\texttt{step7\_orbit\_volume\_negative\_einstein\_collapse.tex}.
\end{LaTeX}
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 8: 原研究交接

状态：Reflect（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

本步从 Strategist 对 Step 7 的两项关键纠正出发，完整读取并检查了 `workspace/notes/step7_orbit_volume_negative_einstein_collapse.tex`、`step7_consolidated_status.md`、`step6_collapsed_unwrapping_route.md`、S0910A01 的覆盖传输与局部刚性笔记，以及 Naber–Zhang 原文的 Theorems 5.1、Propositions 6.4–6.5。首先确认旧证明在写出覆盖次数后将其丢弃，因而不能从底空间绝对亏损直接推出覆盖片小亏损；同时确认已撤回的容量公式仍在支撑区域体积和 cusp 长度推论。相关段落与汇总表均已修复，旧笔记顶部现在明确指向 Step 8 替代文件。

随后检查了 S0910A01 提出的 normal-cover transport 思路。TTCS 两条独立分支核对后，本步采用 Borel 截面、deck 平移不交性与 Bishop–Gromov 比较，建立覆盖层数无关的局部平均传输公式。TTCS 还核对了尺度对齐：在 Naber–Zhang Proposition 6.4 中直接取低平均基点 pᵢ，以 a<1/3 在 B₁(pᵢ) 的局部普适覆盖上应用传输，harmonic chart 与小平均位于同一中心和同一固定尺度。完整推导、显式 Fᵢ、有限 W^{2,p} 传递和体积比例定理写入 `Sessions/S0910A03/workspace/notes/step8_cover_mean_transport_and_model_scope_corrections.md`；独立结果保存在 `trace/ttcs/results/step8_ttcs01_verifier1_integration.md` 与 `step8_ttcs01_verifier2_integration.md`。

本步逐项修正精确模型结论：保留 v''=(3−ρ/2)v 和 nil³ 圆周排除；有限区间排除增加端点 limsup ρ<6；复双曲 cusp 被明确记录为有限体积、无限长度；阿贝尔抛物论证增加精确适配作用、polar 端和有界 v 等输入。`step7_orbit_volume_negative_einstein_collapse.tex` 中关于 Cheeger–Tian 近 Einstein 分解、有限总体积推出 v 有界、容量控制和模型穷尽的段落已删除或改写；`step7_consolidated_status.md` 已重写；`step6_collapsed_unwrapping_route.md` 已更新为覆盖重数问题已解决、固定尺度覆盖几何仍开放。会话组消息 #243、#244 向两位同伴同步了新引理、nil³ 修正和新的剩余问题；S0910A01 随后正式撤回其错误的 3+μ 公式及固定拓扑矛盾。

外部检索与实际阅读补充了 Rong `Knowledge/objects/papers/2211.09998-Collapsed-Manifolds-with-local-Ricci-bounded-Covering-Geometr--4e46d62a6fcb--f76980c4eb0a/object.md`、Jiang–Kong–Xu `Sessions/S0910A03/staging/acquired/Convergence_of_Ricci-limit_spaces_under_bounded_Ricci_curvature_5fddf72b3783b065/part_001.md` 及 canonical nilpotent structure 来源。它们支持一个重要场判断：local rewinding volume、Reifenberg covering geometry 和最大秩是额外几何结构，bounded Ricci 本身不产生一般 nilpotent fibration，也没有找到控制坏覆盖点体积的一般结果。最后读取 Cheeger–Naber Theorem 1.12，确认 S0910A02 的四维正分支非塌缩有限性推论的核心链条成立，但没有采用其尚需另证的 bubble 数量解释。

## 当时的后续问题

以 `workspace/notes/step8_cover_mean_transport_and_model_scope_corrections.md` 为当前负分支入口，发展真正缺失的体积分布机制，而不是继续分类精确 abelian 或 nil³ 模型。首先将假想固定临界 Ishida–LeBrun 序列按局部普适覆盖的 rewinding volume、fibered nilpotency rank、Ricci-limit 模型维数和模型 noncollapsing radius 分层。利用随机体积基点、pointed measured GH 紧性与 quantitative differentiation，研究是否能在统一正体积比例上取得固定尺度的 Euclidean或低维 Ricci-limit 模型。随后集中处理最大秩：尝试证明在这种典型模型片上 rank 缺失会消耗统一的四维尺度不变曲率、Euler/signature 或 monopole 近饱和余量；若能得到这种局部代价，结合固定的全局 L² 曲率预算和 Vitali 型选球可迫使 rank-drop 区域体积消失。若该命题为假，应构造满足 Ric≈−g、固定总容积与固定四维能量轮廓而局部普适覆盖持续塌缩的明确几何模型，以判断当前路线需要怎样重建。

阅读并继承 Rong 2211.09998、Jiang–Kong–Xu 2205.00373、Naber–Zhang 的 rank nonlocalness 与 covering noncollapse 证明，重点区分文献中作为输入的 local covering geometry 与本问题必须从 near-saturation 推出的结构。可探索一个更直接的替代：利用 Codex 缺陷分解中的近平行 monopole/self-dual forms，在小局部平均点上约束 collapsed tangent module，从而迫使 regular collapse 的局部循环达到最大秩，或迫使 rank-drop 区域携带非消失的 ∇form、W⁻ 或拓扑能量。所有推导都应保持固定原尺度；若只能在 rᵢ→0 后展开，Ricci 常数缩放为零，必须另找可在 Ricci-flat 尺度存活的不变量，不能复用 calibrated negative-Einstein germ 矛盾。

同时保留与正分支的互补联系：S0910A02 已确认正夹逼非塌缩族在四维只有有限微分同胚类型，因此 #ₖ(S²×S²) 的紧夹逼序列若存在必定总体积塌缩。比较负分支的新局部平均传输是否能服务于正分支的某个明确代数曲率余量，但不要把缺少 SW 近饱和结构的正分支强行套入当前 Fᵢ。完整目标仍要求所有维数和符号选择；本轮应优先把固定四维负临界族的 inaccessible collapse 变成可证明的局部能量／拓扑命题或明确反模型，从而决定该路线能否产生真正的负分支间隙。
~~~~
