~~~~latex
% Step 10: correction of the Taub--NUT--AdS test and a multiscale
% accessibility / diffuse Pontryagin program for the negative branch.

\section{Scope and corrected quantifier}

Fix a critical Ishida--LeBrun four-manifold and suppose, for contradiction,
that
\[
 \delta_i=\|g_i^{-1}(\Ric_{g_i}+g_i)\|_{L^\infty,\mathrm{op}}\to0.
\]
The global near-equality analysis supplies a collection of nonnegative
curvature/monopole deficits.  Let $F_i$ denote a scalar package containing at
least the Ricci, scalar--Weyl completion, and algebraic lowest-eigenvalue
terms needed for the forbidden-germ passage; its precise monopole components
are those in the Step--8 and Codex notes.  Its integral tends to zero, and
maximal-function selection gives a set of fixed positive volume on which,
for every $0<r\le1$,
\[
 \fint_{B_r(p)}|\Rm_i|^2\le K,
 \qquad \fint_{B_r(p)}F_i\le\varepsilon_i\to0.       \tag{1}
\]
Here and below the curvature norm convention must be fixed; changing between
the curvature-operator and four-index tensor conventions only changes $K$.

The covering domain is part of the geometric choice.  The universal cover of
a large ball, restricted to a smaller sub-ball, is generally not the
universal cover of that sub-ball.  If a short fiber contracts only after a
larger core is included, a smaller buffered domain can still unwrap it.  The
correct fixed-scale question is therefore whether, for some radius bounded
below in terms of $K$, one can first choose a buffered domain and then take a
normal cover which is noncollapsed and has positive harmonic radius.

\section{Taub--NUT--AdS: exact correction}

For
\[
 g_\nu={dr^2\over F_\nu}+(r^2-\nu^2)d\Omega_2^2
 +4\nu^2F_\nu(d\psi+\cos\theta\,d\phi)^2,
\]
\[
 F_\nu={r-\nu\over r+\nu}
 \left(1+{(r-\nu)(r+3\nu)\over3}\right),
\]
the symbolic computation in
\texttt{workspace/scripts/compute\_taub\_nut\_ads\_curvature.py} gives
\[
 \Ric=-g,
 \qquad
 |W|_{(0,4)}^2={32\nu^2(4\nu^2-3)^2\over3(r+\nu)^6}.             \tag{2}
\]
In the coframe orientation used by that script,
\[
 W^+=0,
\]
while
\[
 \Spec(W^-)=\left(
 {2\nu(4\nu^2-3)\over3(r+\nu)^3},
 {2\nu(4\nu^2-3)\over3(r+\nu)^3},
 {-4\nu(4\nu^2-3)\over3(r+\nu)^3}
 \right).                                                       \tag{3}
\]
Thus the family is half-conformally flat, as in the primary Taub--NUT--AdS
source \cite{akbar2002classical}.  Reversing orientation swaps the two
halves.  The four-index norm is four times the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the
nonzero Weyl block.

At the NUT,
\[
 |W|_{(0,4)}^2={ (4\nu^2-3)^2\over6\nu^4}
 \sim{3\over2\nu^4}.                                          \tag{4}
\]
The NUT is smooth for each $\nu$, but its curvature is not uniform as
$\nu\to0$.  The complete-orbit radial volume density is
\[
 {dV\over dr}=32\pi^2\nu(r^2-\nu^2),                            \tag{5}
\]
and the cumulative full-Weyl energy is
\[
 E_\nu^W(R)={32\pi^2(4\nu^2-3)^2\over9}
 { (R-\nu)^2(R^2+6R\nu+17\nu^2)\over(R+\nu)^4}.                 \tag{6}
\]
Consequently $E_\nu^W(\infty)\to32\pi^2$.  On a fixed physical
neighborhood reaching the NUT, volume is $O(\nu)$ but Weyl energy tends to a
positive constant, so its mean curvature energy diverges like $\nu^{-1}$.
On the NUT scale it diverges like $\nu^{-4}$.  This corrects the Step--9
statement that the all-radius curvature maximal function stayed bounded.

Let $p_\nu$ have distance $1/2$ from the NUT.  For radii at most $1/3$, its
balls lie in a fixed annulus; there $|W|^2=O(\nu^2)$ and their volumes are
$\Theta(\nu)$.  If instead a ball radius exceeds $1/2$, it sees the NUT core
and its curvature mean diverges.  Moreover:
\begin{itemize}
\item the universal cover of a large domain containing the NUT does not
unwrap the short Hopf circle, because that circle contracts through the NUT;
\item if one first chooses a fixed buffered radius $R_0<1/2$ around $p_\nu$,
the domain misses the NUT, lies over a contractible annular base patch, and
its universal cover unwraps the circle at a fixed scale.
\end{itemize}
Hence Taub--NUT--AdS refutes neither the adjustable-buffer covering question
nor the simultaneous input (1).

On the unwrapped annulus, with $z=2\nu\psi$,
\[
 g_\nu\to {dr^2\over1+r^2/3}+r^2d\Omega_2^2+(1+r^2/3)dz^2,
                                                                    \tag{7}
\]
which is real hyperbolic four-space of sectional curvature $-1/3$.  Thus
$s=-4$, $W^+=0$, and
\[
 (s+8\sqrt6|W^+|)^2=16.                                       \tag{8}
\]
The standard NUT profile cannot occur on the calibrated good set.  Near its
core curvature is too large for (1); on fixed annuli its scalar--Weyl deficit
is macroscopically positive; the calibrated Weyl magnitude occurs only in a
transition shell of radius comparable to $\nu^{1/3}$ and not on all centered
scales.

\section{Homothetic scaling of the forbidden germ}

If $\widehat g=a^2g$, then the $(0,2)$ Ricci tensor and the $(1,3)$ Weyl
tensor are unchanged, but the corresponding endomorphisms scale by $a^{-2}$:
\[
 \widehat g^{-1}\Ric_{\widehat g}=a^{-2}g^{-1}\Ric_g,
 \qquad W^\pm_{\widehat g}=a^{-2}W^\pm_g.                       \tag{9}
\]
Therefore the calibrated germ at negative Einstein scale $\kappa>0$ is
\[
 \Ric=-\kappa g,
 \qquad
 \Spec(W^+)=\left(-{\kappa\over6},{\kappa\over12},{\kappa\over12}\right).
                                                                    \tag{10}
\]
The constant-spectrum projector identity gives $\nabla W^+=0$, while the
Einstein--Weyl identity requires
\[
 |\nabla W^+|^2={\kappa^3\over16}>0.                            \tag{11}
\]
Thus the contradiction survives every fixed rescaling.  It degenerates only
when the available covering radius tends to zero and hence $\kappa\to0$.
The Step--9 phrase that the numerical spectrum was invariant under homothety
is withdrawn.

\section{The corrected fixed-scale accessibility target}

For a buffered scale $\rho$ and constants $A>1$, $0<\eta<1$, define
\[
 \Gamma(p;\rho,A,\eta)=\Image\left[
 \pi_1(B_{\eta\rho}(p))\longrightarrow\pi_1(B_{A\rho}(p))
 \right].                                                       \tag{12}
\]
Changing $A\rho$ changes the group: enlarging the domain can kill a short
fiber by admitting a contraction core.  Naber--Zhang's result
\cite{naber2016topology}, and the related buffered normal-cover statement in
\cite{huang2020ricci}, show that a low-dimensional GH model, nondegenerate
model scale, and maximal rank of (12) yield cover noncollapse and harmonic
radius at a definite smaller scale.  Combined with normal-cover mean
transport, (1), and (10)--(11), any positive-volume set with this package is
excluded.

A theorem of the following strength would settle this fixed-topology negative
branch:

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Calibrated fixed-scale cover theorem.}
For each finite $K$, there are fixed buffer and regularity constants such
that every sequence satisfying (1) contains, at a good point, a scale
$\rho\ge r_*(K)>0$ and a buffered normal cover chosen after fixing
$B_{A\rho}(p)$, whose lifted smaller ball has a uniform four-dimensional
volume ratio and harmonic radius.  The mean-transfer radius must fit inside
the chosen buffer (for example a $3a$ core as in Step 8).

\medskip
Equivalently, one may prove a multiscale rank-recovery statement: persistent
rank loss for every $\rho\in[r_*(K),1]$ forces either a positive centered
mean of $F$, model-scale degeneration, or a quantified curvature/topology
cost.  Taub--NUT supplies only a single threshold at the distance to its core;
below that threshold rank recovers.  A genuine countermodel must arrange a
nested or diffuse family of contraction/twist mechanisms at every fixed
scale while maintaining the calibrated Weyl profile and (1).

\section{Diffuse Pontryagin density}

Let $E=\Lambda^2_+M$ and let $A_+^{LC}$ be its induced $SO(3)$ connection.
The Chern--Weil representative in our convention is
\[
 \rho_+={1\over4\pi^2}\left(
 {s^2\over24}+2|W^+|^2-{1\over2}|\Ric^\circ|^2
 \right),
 \qquad \int_M\rho_+\,d\mu=2\chi+3\tau={2A\over3}.             \tag{13}
\]
The calibrated profile gives the stronger localizable fact
\[
 \left\|\rho_+-{3\over16\pi^2}\right\|_{L^1}\to0.             \tag{14}
\]
Consequently, for every measurable $U_i$,
\[
 \int_{U_i}\rho_{+,i}\,d\mu_i
 ={3\over16\pi^2}\Vol(U_i)+o(1),                               \tag{15}
\]
where the same global $o(1)$ bounds the error for every $U_i$.  Thus
characteristic mass follows volume.  It cannot be assigned only to
vanishing-volume NUT cores, and counting integer local charges is not the
correct first move.

On a regular collapse region choose a basic or split comparison connection
$B$ and put $a=A_+^{LC}-B$, $A_t=B+ta$.  For the normalized quadratic
invariant polynomial $P$,
\[
 P(F_A)-P(F_B)=dT_P(A,B),                                      \tag{16}
\]
\[
 T_P(A,B)=2P(a,F_B)+P(a,d_Ba)+{1\over3}P(a,[a,a]).              \tag{17}
\]
If $B$ is pulled back from a base of dimension at most three,
$P(F_B)=0$ as a four-form.  Hence on $U$,
\[
 \int_U\rho_+\,d\mu=\int_{\partial U}T_P(A,B).                \tag{18}
\]
This is a continuous Chern--Simons flux, not a local integer without extra
boundary data.  Equations (15) and (18) show that a positive-volume collapsed
bulk must support persistent non-basic connection data or persistent flux
through its interfaces.

For an invariant rank-one circle collapse write, using a unit vertical
one-form $\eta$,
\[
 F_A=F_H+\eta\wedge\Xi,
 \qquad \Xi=\iota_VF_A.                                       \tag{19}
\]
Horizontal dimension is three, so
\[
 P(F_A)=2\eta\wedge P(\Xi,F_H).                                \tag{20}
\]
In a standard inner-product normalization this gives the robust inequality
\[
 \left|\int_U\rho_+\,d\mu\right|^2
 \le C_P\left(\int_U|F_H|^2\right)
          \left(\int_U|\Xi|^2\right).                          \tag{21}
\]
If the horizontal curvature mean is bounded by $K$, (15) yields
\[
 \fint_U|\Xi|^2\ge c(K)-o(1).                                 \tag{22}
\]
Thus the calibrated bulk cannot be basic: mixed vertical--horizontal
curvature survives at order one in mean.

This still does not imply that ordinary fiber holonomy is far from the
identity.  If the fiber length is $\ell$ and
$A=A_H+\Phi\vartheta$ with $\eta=\ell\vartheta$, then schematically
\[
 \Xi=\ell^{-1}D_H\Phi+\mathcal E_{\rm O'Neill}.                 \tag{23}
\]
The ordinary holonomy may vary only by $O(\ell)$ while its scaled logarithm
has order-one derivative.  Therefore diffuse Pontryagin mass can in principle
be carried throughout a collapsed bulk by scaled holonomy, O'Neill tensors,
nil commutators, or vertical frame twisting.  It does not by itself prove
fiber survival in the buffered fundamental group.

The next analytic object is an estimate decomposing the mixed curvature into
fixed-scale accessibility and contraction/twist costs,
\[
 \int_U|\Xi|^2
 \le C\big(E_{\rm accessible}+E_{\rm fill}
                 +E_{\rm O'Neill/nil}\big)+o(1),               \tag{24}
\]
with $E_{\rm fill}$ measuring curvature needed to contract short fibers in a
buffered domain.  Combined with (22), such an estimate would force a positive
volume of fixed-scale accessible points unless the filling/twisting terms
remain diffuse.  The alternative is equally informative: a counterexample
must solve a reduced mixed-curvature equation with diffuse Chern--Simons flux,
not merely attach finitely many NUT caps.

\section{Implications beyond the negative test family}

This step does not settle either normalized branch.  It repairs a false
route exclusion and identifies a sharper common collapse question.  The
positive branch also cannot derive pointwise curvature control from a
$C^0$ Ricci defect: the opposite-warping Calder\'on--Zygmund spike constructed
by S0910A02 keeps the Ricci defect small while its mixed Riemann curvature
spikes.  Thus both signs require harmonic-coordinate/cover methods,
$L^p$ control, smoothing, or weak test-field identities rather than a direct
$L^\infty$ Ricci-to-curvature implication.

Finally, the logical reduction is
\[
 Q_n\Longleftrightarrow P_n^+\lor P_n^-.
\]
To refute $Q_n$ one must refute both normalized branches in the same
dimension, but the two witnessing manifolds or sequences need not be the
same.  Earlier notes requiring a single manifold to realize both failures
imposed an unnecessary strengthening and are superseded on this point.
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 11: 原研究交接

状态：Process（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

本步从 Strategist 的各向异性指导出发，建立了静态圆约化公式并发现了关键符号/因子错误。初始推导给出 W⁺ = 2J(h - I/3)，要求校准 h = (3/8, 3/8, 1/4)。TTCS 验证器通过逐指标重算发现正确公式为 Spec(W⁺) = {1/3 - η_i}，要求校准 h = (1/2, 1/4, 1/4)。余同一性一协同更强：a'' = a/4 vs a'' = a/2（相对间隙 1/2）。扭曲符号修正：tr(h) = 1 + ℓ²|F|²/4 > 1。关键的近 NUT 修正：h 和扭曲修正均发散并在光滑总曲率中相消，静态公式不支配 NUT 附近，NUT 不必迫使 W⁺ → 0。

有效结论为纤维存活二择：(S) 纤维在固定缓冲尺度存活 → 覆盖图 → 禁止 Einstein germ → 矛盾；(D) 纤维在每个固定尺度内死亡，需持续高扭曲 ℓ²|F|² ≥ c > 0 维持校准各向异性。Pontryagin 密度下界对所有 Ric = -g 自动成立（自对偶性），不具区分力；区分特征是 W⁺ 各向异性（本征值结构）。

向会话组发送了修正后的公式和二择结论（msg #257）。A01 确认 Taub-NUT-AdS 多尺度计算，发展秩一 Cartan 结构。A02 的环面行列式计算显示正交传递性（扭曲常数在退化边处消失），直接联系我们的二择案 (D)。

所有结果写入 workspace/notes/step11_circle_reduction_anisotropy_and_fiber_survival.tex、corrected_circle_reduction.py 和 step11_consolidated_status.md。先前的 circle_reduction_weyl.py 和 verify_static_incompatibility.py 中的公式已被修正版取代。

## 当时的后续问题

整合三个会话的互补成果并确定负支高扭曲案 (D) 的最有价值攻击路线。当前状态：

(1) A03 建立了修正的静态圆约化 Spec(W⁺) = {1/3 - η_i}，唯一兼容的常本征值静态 Einstein 为 W⁺ = 0，纤维存活二择已陈述但案 (D) 未排除。近 NUT 修正表明 h 与扭曲均发散，净 W⁺ 取决于精确抵消。

(2) A01 发展了秩一 Λ²₊ 联络代数的 Cartan 结构方程和一阶射流计算，支持弥散混合曲率图景。确认 Taub-NUT-AdS 不能反驳可调整缓冲覆盖。

(3) A02 的环面行列式给出 Δ_B w = (|F|²/2 + 2)w（负 Einstein）和正交传递性引理：退化边处扭曲常数消失。若可推广到近似设定，则案 (D) 的纤维死亡点附近变为近静态，静态不相容启动。A02 还有分离杆模型 Vol ≥ 16π² 的 AM-GM 估计。

关键决策：(a) 优先发展 A02 正交传递性向近似度量的推广，将其与纤维存活二择结合，尝试排除案 (D)？(b) 转向正支或高维，寻找互补方向？(c) 直接在关键 Ishida-LeBrun 流形上计算具体度量序列，测试案 (D) 的可行性？
~~~~

~~~~latex
% Step 11: Circle reduction of W+ anisotropy and the fiber survival dichotomy
% S0910A03 Agent2 (Constructor) — Explore
%
% This note develops the static circle reduction of W+ for the
% negative-branch calibrated sequence, corrects the initial formula
% (following TTCS verification), and establishes the key dichotomy
% connecting W+ anisotropy to fixed-scale fiber survival.
%
% Supersedes: the uncorrected formulas in circle_reduction_weyl.py and
% verify_static_incompatibility.py.  Corrected script: corrected_circle_reduction.py.
%
% STEP 12 REPAIR: the static formula in Sections 1--2 remains valid, as does
% the spherical cohomogeneity-one calibrated exclusion.  The claimed general
% static rigidity, the fiber-survival/high-twist dichotomy, and the inference
% from toric orthogonal transitivity to a static chosen circle are withdrawn.
% Small ell^2|F|^2 does not control ell*nabla F or (nabla ell)*F, and quotient
% geometry was not derived.  See workspace/notes/step12_reduced_equations_accessibility.md.

\section{Static circle reduction of $W^+$: corrected formula}

Let $(M^4,g)$ be an oriented Riemannian four-manifold with a static free
circle action, so $g=q+\ell^2d\psi^2$ where $q=g_B$ is the base metric on
$B^3$ and $\ell:B\to\R_{>0}$ is the orbit-length function.  If $\Ric_g=-g$,
the warped-product Ricci equations give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:static-einstein}
 \Ric_B=h-g_B,\qquad \Delta_B\ell=\ell,\qquad
 h\coloneqq\ell^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_B\ell,\quad \tr h=1.
\end{equation}
In the adapted orthonormal frame $e_1,e_2,e_3$ for $B$ and $e_4=\ell^{-1}\partial_\psi$,
the self-dual 2-forms are
\[
 \omega_1=\frac{e^{12}+e^{34}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \omega_2=\frac{e^{13}-e^{24}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \omega_3=\frac{e^{14}+e^{23}}{\sqrt2}.
\]
The static warped-product curvature gives $R_{abcd}=R^B_{abcd}$,
$R_{a4b4}=-h_{ab}$, $R_{abc4}=0$.  In three dimensions,
$R^B_{abcd}$ is determined by $\Ric_B=h-I$ and $s_B=-2$.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Proposition (Corrected static reduction).}
\emph{The curvature operator on $\Lambda^2_+$ in the Besse convention is}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rhat-static}
 \widehat R_+=
 \begin{pmatrix}
  -h_{33}&h_{23}&-h_{13}\\
  h_{23}&-h_{22}&h_{12}\\
  -h_{13}&h_{12}&-h_{11}
 \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
\emph{Consequently,}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:spec-rhat}
 \boxed{\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat R_+)=-\operatorname{Spec}(h),}
\end{equation}
\emph{and}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wplus-static}
 W^+=\widehat R_++\frac13I,
 \qquad
 \boxed{\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)
  =\left\{\frac13-\eta_i\right\}_{i=1,2,3},}
\end{equation}
\emph{where $\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3$ are the eigenvalues of $h$.}

\begin{proof}
For the diagonal entries, use $\tr h=1$ and the three-dimensional identity
$K_{ab}=(h_a+h_b-h_c-1)/\ldots$ to simplify:
\[
 (\widehat R_+)_{11}=\frac12(K_{12}-h_{33})
 =\frac{h_{11}+h_{22}-3h_{33}-1}{4}=-h_{33},
\]
where the last step uses $h_{11}+h_{22}=1-h_{33}$.  Similarly for the other
diagonal entries.  Off-diagonal entries use $R^B_{1213}=\Ric^B_{23}=h_{23}$
and $R_{a4b4}=-h_{ab}$.  The eigenvalue statement follows because the matrix
\eqref{eq:rhat-static} is conjugate to $-h$ by the index permutation
$1\leftrightarrow3$ (a diagonal orthogonal transformation).
\end{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Calibrated Hessian spectrum.}
The calibrated self-dual Weyl spectrum
$(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12})$ requires
\begin{equation}\label{eq:h-calibrated}
 \boxed{\operatorname{Spec}(h)=\left(\frac12,\frac14,\frac14\right),
 \qquad \tr h=1.}
\end{equation}
The simple $W^+$ eigenvalue $-1/6$ corresponds to the large Hessian
eigenvalue $1/2$; the double eigenvalue $1/12$ corresponds to the
smaller pair $1/4$.  This means the warping function $\ell$ has
\emph{stronger} curvature in the direction singled out by the simple
$W^+$ eigenline.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Verification.}
For constant curvature $K=-1/3$: $h=\frac13I$, $\widehat R_+=-\frac13I$,
$W^+=0$.  Script \texttt{corrected\_circle\_reduction.py} confirms both
the isotropic and calibrated cases.

\section{Static cohomogeneity-one incompatibility}

For $g=dt^2+a(t)^2g_{S^2}+\ell(t)^2d\psi^2$ with $\Ric=-g$, let
$u=\ell''/\ell$ and $v=a'\ell'/(a\ell)$.  Then $h=\diag(u,v,v)$ and
\[
 \Spec(W^+)=\left(\frac13-v,\frac13-v,\frac13-u\right).
\]
The calibrated target gives $u=\frac12$, $v=\frac14$.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Proposition (Static ODE incompatibility).}
\emph{There is no smooth cohomogeneity-one static circle Einstein metric
with constant calibrated $W^+$ spectrum.}

\begin{proof}
From the radial Einstein equation:
\[
 a''=\frac{a(1-u)}{2}=\frac{a}{4}.
\]
From the angular Einstein equation together with the calibrated $v$:
\[
 (a')^2=1+\frac{a^2}{2}.
\]
Differentiating: $a''=a/2$, contradicting $a''=a/4$.  The relative gap is
$|a/2-a/4|/(a/2)=1/2$.
\end{proof}

\noindent\textbf{Scope of the ODE calculation.}
If constant $u,v$ are allowed to float \emph{within this spherical
cohomogeneity-one ansatz}, the same elimination gives $u=v$.  Combined with
$u+2v=1$, this forces $u=v=\frac13$ and hence $W^+=0$.  This is not a
classification of general static Einstein circle metrics.  For example,
$\mathbb H^2\times\mathbb H^2$, using polar circles in the first factor, has
$\operatorname{Spec}(h)=(1,0,0)$ and constant
$\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)=(-2/3,1/3,1/3)$ up to orientation.

\section{Twisted reduction and sign correction}

For a general Kaluza--Klein metric $g=q+\ell^2\theta^2$, $\theta=d\psi+A$,
$F=dA$, the vertical Einstein equation becomes
\[
 -\frac{\Delta_B\ell}{\ell}+\frac{\ell^2}{4}F_{ab}F^{ab}=-1,
\]
giving
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tr-h-twisted}
 \boxed{\tr h=1+\frac{\ell^2}{4}F_{ab}F^{ab}\ge1,}
\end{equation}
with equality only when $F=0$.  This corrects the earlier sign error;
twist \emph{increases} $\tr h$ above the static value $1$.

The horizontal Einstein equation is modified to
\[
 \Ric_B=h+\frac{\ell^2}{2}(F^2)_{\rm sym}-g_B,
\]
and the full curvature operator on $\Lambda^2_+$ acquires additional terms:
\[
 \widehat R_+=\widehat R_+^{\rm static}+\widehat R_+^{\rm twist}.
\]
For the Taub--NUT--AdS family,
$\widehat R_+^{\rm static}+\widehat R_+^{\rm twist}=-\frac13I$
(i.e., $W^+=0$ in the half-flat orientation).

\section{Near-NUT behavior: corrected analysis}

A critical correction from the TTCS verification: near a smooth NUT
where $\ell\to0$, the quotient-base geometry degenerates.  Setting
$d=r-\nu$ (distance from the NUT in the Taub--NUT--AdS radial coordinate),
\[
 \ell^2\sim2\nu d,\qquad
 h_{\rm ang}\sim\frac{1}{8\nu d}\to\infty,\qquad
 \ell^2|F|^2\sim\frac{1}{2\nu d}\to\infty.
\]
Both the static Hessian contribution and the twist correction diverge
individually while canceling in the total (smooth) curvature.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Consequence.}
The static formula $W^+\approx\frac13I-h$ does \emph{not} dominate near
a smooth NUT.  The net $W^+$ depends on the precise balance between
divergent Hessian and twist terms.  In particular, it is \emph{not}
correct to conclude that ``$W^+\to0$ near any smooth NUT.''  A
NUT with appropriate twist could in principle produce any $W^+$
eigenvalue structure.

This removes one initially proposed mechanism (NUT forces isotropic $W^+$,
creating calibrated deficit) and replaces it with the more precise dichotomy
below.

\section{Withdrawn fiber-survival/high-twist dichotomy}

The following division was proposed by the TTCS generator but is \emph{not
established}; it is retained only as a record of the superseded proposal.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Superseded proposed division.}
The following alternatives were conjectured for the calibrated good set, but
the asserted implication in the second item was not proved:

\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textbf{(S)}] \textbf{Fiber survival.}
\emph{The circle fiber class survives at a fixed buffer scale
$\rho\ge\rho_0(K)>0$: a buffered normal cover at that scale unwraps
the fiber, the cover is noncollapsed, and the mean-transport carries
the calibrated deficit.  This produces the forbidden calibrated Einstein
germ (Steps~5--6), giving a contradiction.}

\item[\textbf{(D)}] \textbf{Fiber death with high twist.}
\emph{The fiber contracts within every fixed buffer scale.  The static
incompatibility forces}
\[
 \ell^2|F|^2=\tau\ge c_Q>0
\]
\emph{on a definite fraction of the region; otherwise the leading-order
$W^+$ would be forced toward $W^+=0$ (static isotropic), contradicting
the calibrated deficit bound.}
\end{enumerate}

The fiber-length function $\ell(p)$ can be arbitrarily small at a good
point (a conformal rescaling $\ell\mapsto\varepsilon\ell$ does not change
$h=\Hess\ell/\ell$).  The curvature mean bounds $h$, not $\ell$.

In the non-degenerate case (\textbf{S}), the Harnack estimate for the
positive eigenfunction equation $\Delta_B\ell=(1+\tau/4)\ell$ gives
\[
 \sup_{B_{R/2}}\ell\le C_H\inf_{B_{R/2}}\ell,\qquad
 |\nabla\log\ell|\le C_H/R,
\]
provided the base geometry, twist energy $\tau$, and base harmonic
radius are controlled.  Under these conditions, a positive fiber length
at a good point remains positive throughout a fixed-radius neighborhood,
supplying the buffer domain for the covering chart.

Case \textbf{(D)} requires a diffuse mechanism:
$\ell^2|F|^2\ge c>0$ must persist on a positive-volume subset to maintain
the calibrated anisotropy.  This ``scaled twist energy'' acts as a source
of non-basic curvature.

\section{Relation to Pontryagin and accessibility}

The Strategist's correction clarifies that the positive lower bound on
$|\Xi|^2=|\iota_VF_{A_+}|^2$ (from the calibrated Pontryagin density,
Step~10) is \emph{not discriminating}: for any Einstein metric with
$\Ric=-g$, the Levi-Civita connection on $\Lambda^2_+$ has self-dual
curvature, giving $|\iota_VF|^2=|F|^2/2$ automatically.  The isotropic
scalar contribution $s^2/24$ provides $88.9\%$ of the calibrated
characteristic density; the anisotropic $2|W^+|^2$ term adds only
$11.1\%$.

The \emph{distinguishing} information is the eigenvalue structure:
the calibrated curvature operator on $\Lambda^2_+$ has spectrum
$(-1/2,-1/4,-1/4)$, while the isotropic (hyperbolic) spectrum is
$(-1/3,-1/3,-1/3)$.  The anisotropy
\[
 |W^+|^2=1/24
\]
is the correct measure of deviation from the benign Einstein background,
not the total characteristic density.

\section{Peer results and integration}

S0910A01 (Step~12): independently verified the Taub--NUT--AdS multiscale
computation and agrees that the target is multiscale rank recovery, not
NUT charge counting.  Their rank-one Cartan structure equations support
the diffuse mixed-curvature picture.

S0910A02 (Step~12): developed toric determinant calculations for $T^2$-invariant
metrics.  Key finding: $\tr_h\Ric^V=-\Delta_Bw/w+|F|_h^2/2$ with
$w=\sqrt{\det h}$, leading to $\Delta_Bw=(|F|^2/2-2\lambda)w$.
For $\lambda=-1$: $\Delta_Bw=(|F|^2/2+2)w$, giving strong subharmonicity
of the orbit-volume function.  Their orthogonal transitivity lemma
(conserved twist constants vanish at degeneration edges) is relevant to
our dichotomy: if twist vanishes near bolts/edges, the remaining collapse
is static and incompatible with the calibrated spectrum.

\section{Current research position (repaired in Step 12)}

\textbf{What is established:}
\begin{itemize}
\item The corrected static circle reduction formula
$\Spec(W^+)=\{1/3-\eta_i\}$, verified against constant curvature,
$\mathbb H^2\times\mathbb H^2$, and Taub--NUT--AdS.
\item The calibrated spectrum is incompatible with the displayed spherical
cohomogeneity-one static ansatz.  General calibrated exclusion comes instead
from the Step 6 projector/Derdzi\'nski Einstein-germ argument.
\item Buffered fiber survival plus a supplied controlled cover chart leads to
the forbidden germ.  No converse from failure of accessibility to high
$\ell^2|F|^2$ has been proved.
\item The Pontryagin density is not discriminating; the $W^+$ anisotropy is.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What remains open:}
\begin{itemize}
\item Can derivative twisting $\ell\nabla F+(\nabla\ell)F$ or quotient
geometry degeneration prevent every fixed-scale buffered chart while the
calibrated profile and curvature means remain controlled?
\item Can the weighted quotient structure inherited from four-dimensional
Ricci bounds be upgraded, together with the complete reduced equations, to
fixed-scale cover reconstruction?  The earlier Harnack argument assumed the
ordinary base control it was meant to obtain.
\item The positive branch, higher dimensions, and Lean formalization.
\end{itemize}

\section{Files and references}
\begin{itemize}
\item Corrected script: \texttt{workspace/scripts/corrected\_circle\_reduction.py}
\item TTCS generator: \texttt{trace/ttcs/results/step11\_ttcs01\_generator1\_integration.md}
\item TTCS verifier: \texttt{trace/ttcs/results/step11\_ttcs01\_verifier1\_integration.md}
\item Previous notes: Steps~6, 9, 10 (local obstruction, Weitzenb\"ock, Pontryagin)
\end{itemize}
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 11 consolidated status

> **Step 12 repair.** The static formula and spherical cohomogeneity-one calculation remain valid. The general static-rigidity wording and the fiber-survival/high-twist dichotomy below are superseded: `H^2 x H^2` is a static constant-spectrum counterexample to the former, while small scaled twist does not control derivative twisting or quotient geometry. Toric orthogonal transitivity also does not make a chosen Hopf circle static. See `step12_reduced_equations_accessibility.md`.

## Corrections applied this step

### Static circle reduction formula
The initial formula W+ = 2J(h - I/3) was WRONG by a factor/sign.

CORRECTED (verified by TTCS and computation):
- R_hat_+ on Lambda^2_+ has Spec = -Spec(h), where h = Hess(ell)/ell
- W+ = R_hat_+ + (1/3)I, so **Spec(W+) = {1/3 - eta_i}**
- Calibrated: h = (1/2, 1/4, 1/4), NOT (3/8, 3/8, 1/4)
- Script: `workspace/scripts/corrected_circle_reduction.py`

### Twist sign
tr(h) = 1 + ell^2|F|^2/4 > 1 under nonzero twist (corrected from < 1).

### Near-NUT behavior
Both h and twist corrections diverge near a smooth NUT. They cancel in the 
total smooth curvature. The static formula does NOT dominate near the NUT.
This invalidates the claim that "NUTs force isotropic W+."

## New results

### Static cohomogeneity-one incompatibility (verified)
For a static Einstein circle metric with constant calibrated spectrum:
- Einstein E1 gives a'' = a/4
- Einstein E2 + differentiation gives a'' = a/2
- CONTRADICTION with gap a/4 (relative error 1/2)

Within the displayed spherical cohomogeneity-one ansatz, the only compatible constant-eigenvalue solution is u = v = 1/3 (W+ = 0). This is not a general static classification.

### Superseded TTCS proposal
Buffered fiber survival plus a controlled cover chart still leads to the forbidden Einstein germ. It has **not** been shown that failure of accessibility forces `ell^2|F|^2 >= c`: `ell nabla F`, `(nabla ell)F`, and quotient degeneration remain possible, so there is no established case (D).

### Pontryagin non-discrimination (Strategist correction)
The Ξ lower bound from the Pontryagin density is automatic for ALL Ric=-g 
(by self-duality of the connection curvature on Lambda^2_+). The isotropic 
scalar part provides 88.9% of the calibrated density. The distinguishing 
feature is the W+ ANISOTROPY (eigenvalue structure), not the density.

## Integration with peers

- A01 (Step 12): Confirms Taub-NUT-AdS multiscale computation. Developing 
  rank-one Cartan structure equations for the Lambda^2_+ connection algebra.
  One-jet computations support diffuse mixed-curvature picture.

- A02 (Step 12): Toric determinant calculation with 
  tr_h Ric^V = -Delta_B w/w + |F|^2_h/2. Its toric orthogonal-transitivity result concerns integrability of the 2-plane perpendicular to full torus orbits; it does not remove the connection curvature of an individual circle reduction.

## Research position

The four-dimensional negative-branch collapse analysis has three remaining 
mechanisms:

1. **Case (S) with noncollapse + maximal rank**: EXCLUDED by the forbidden 
   calibrated Einstein germ (Steps 5-6), assuming buffer-scale covering 
   charts exist.

2. **Case (D) with high twist**: NOT YET EXCLUDED. Requires diffuse 
   ell^2|F|^2 >= c > 0, which means persistent scaled holonomy/O'Neill 
   curvature. Global constraints (topology, energy budget) may exclude 
   this but the argument is not constructed.

3. **NUT-type with contractible fibers**: NOT YET EXCLUDED in general.
   Taub-NUT-AdS shows standard NUTs have diverging curvature near the 
   core and calibrated deficit 16 on the unwrapped annulus. But the 
   corrected near-NUT analysis shows that general smooth NUTs could 
   potentially maintain any W+ structure through cancellation of 
   divergent h and twist terms.

The positive branch, higher dimensions, and Lean formalization remain open.
~~~~

## Exact Task

Consider a closed oriented Einstein 4-manifold (M, g) with Ric = -g that is collapsing with circle fibers of length function ℓ. The self-dual Weyl operator in the static circle reduction is W+ = 2J(h - I/3) where h = Hess(ℓ)/ℓ, plus twist corrections that are O(ℓ²|F|²) where F = dA is the connection curvature. The calibrated spectrum (-1/6, 1/12, 1/12) requires h eigenvalues (3/8, 3/8, 1/4) in the static case, but the ONLY constant-eigenvalue static Einstein circle metric has h = I/3 (i.e., W+ = 0). This is the static incompatibility.

Near a smooth NUT (ℓ → 0), twist corrections vanish as O(ℓ²), so the static formula dominates: W+ → 2J(h - I/3) with h constrained to the isotropic value by Einstein. This means the calibrated anisotropy cannot persist into the NUT core.

Develop a rigorous argument connecting this anisotropy constraint to fiber survival at a fixed buffer scale on the calibrated good set. Specifically:

1. For a good point p (bounded curvature mean at all scales ≤ 1, small calibrated deficit), can the fiber length ℓ(p) be arbitrarily small? The Riemann tensor in the e_a ∧ e_4 directions contains h_{ab} = Hess(ℓ)_{ab}/ℓ, which diverges if ℓ → 0 with |∇ℓ| bounded. Use the curvature mean bound to derive a lower bound on ℓ(p) at good points.

2. If ℓ(p) ≥ ℓ₀ > 0, then the fiber survives in a ball B_R(p) of fixed radius (from the slow variation of ℓ implied by the curvature bound). This gives a buffer-scale covering chart, which transports the calibrated deficit and produces the forbidden Einstein germ.

3. Alternatively, if ℓ(p) can be small at a good point, show that the static incompatibility forces a positive calibrated deficit or excessive curvature on B_R(p), using the fact that calibrated W+ requires substantial twist energy (O(ℓ²|F|²) ≥ c), while the total twist energy is controlled by the topology.

The scientific product should be a clear mechanism connecting the W+ anisotropy, the circle-reduction Hessian, and fiber survival, leading to a conditional or unconditional exclusion of circle-collapse on the calibrated good set.

## Integrated Scientific Memo

## 结论：应控制的是纤维的固定尺度存活，而不是 \(\ell(p)\) 本身

设正则圆塌缩区写成
\[
g=q+\ell^2\theta^2,\qquad \theta=d\psi+A,\qquad F=dA,
\]
并令
\[
h=\ell^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_q\ell,\qquad Z=\ell F,\qquad \tau=|Z|^2=\ell^2|F|^2 .
\]
在一致的 Kaluza–Klein 约定下，
\[
R_{a4b4}=-h_{ab}+\frac14 Z_{ac}Z_b{}^c,
\]
而
\[
W^+=2J\!\left(h-\frac13I\right)+Q(Z,\nabla Z,\nabla\log\ell),
\qquad |Q|\lesssim \tau
\]
在近静态、受控约化区域成立。静态校准要求
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(h)=\left(\frac38,\frac38,\frac14\right),
\]
且
\[
\left|h-\frac13I\right|
=\left|\operatorname{diag}\left(\frac1{24},\frac1{24},-\frac1{12}\right)\right|
=\frac1{4\sqrt6}.
\]
因此校准各向异性与静态各向同性 \(h=I/3\) 之间存在固定间隙。

不过，下述推论是错误的：
\[
\fint_{B_r(p)}|\Rm|^2\le K\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell(p)\ge \ell_0(K).
\]

例如
\[
g_\varepsilon
=dt^2+e^{2t/\sqrt3}(dx^2+dy^2+\varepsilon^2d\psi^2)
\]
局部具有 \(\Ric=-g_\varepsilon\)、固定有界曲率和
\[
\ell_\varepsilon=\varepsilon e^{t/\sqrt3}\to0,\qquad
F=0,\qquad h=\frac13I,\qquad W^+=0.
\]
乘法缩放 \(\ell\mapsto\varepsilon\ell\) 不改变 \(h=\Hess\ell/\ell\)。所以曲率均值只能控制无量纲量 \(h,\ell F\) 等，不能控制纤维的绝对长度。

真正可用的命题是：

\[
\boxed{\text{校准好点不能同时具有低扭曲和固定尺度内的纤维死亡。}}
\]

---

## 1. 固定缓冲尺度上的存活替代绝对长度下界

定义纤维存活半径 \(a(p)\)：它是使圆纤维在预先选定的缓冲域
\(B_{A\rho}(p)\) 中仍代表非平凡局部基本群元素的最大尺度。这里必须先选缓冲域，再取正规覆盖；扩大缓冲域可能纳入 NUT 核并杀死纤维类。

若
\[
a(p)\ge R_0>0,
\]
则即使 \(\ell(p)\to0\)，缓冲域的正规覆盖仍可把圆方向展开。对于具有受控三维基底几何的纯秩一塌缩，展开后较小球满足
\[
\Vol B_{cR_0}(\tilde p)\ge v_0R_0^4.
\]
好点的均值估计通过正规覆盖传递：
\[
\fint_{B_r(\tilde p)}|\widetilde{\Rm}|^2\le C K,\qquad
\fint_{B_r(\tilde p)}\widetilde F_{\rm cal}\le C\varepsilon_i,
\qquad r\le cR_0.
\]
在有非塌缩、Ricci 控制及适用的调和半径/\(\varepsilon\)-正则性条件时，可取得光滑 Einstein 极限
\[
\Ric=-g,\qquad
\Spec(W^+)=\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right).
\]
这与局部投影算子障碍矛盾：常谱和 \(\delta W^+=0\) 给出
\[
\nabla W^+=0,
\]
而 Einstein–Weyl 恒等式要求
\[
|\nabla W^+|^2=\frac1{16}.
\]

因此
\[
\boxed{\text{任何校准好点若在固定尺度上保留圆纤维，就产生禁戒 Einstein germ。}}
\]

这里不能只凭“局部 universal cover”自动断言非塌缩；还须有正则圆纤维结构、受控基底尺度和最大秩条件。这正是缓冲正规覆盖表述的必要性。

---

## 2. 低扭曲纤维死亡造成曲率或校准亏损

假设纤维在每个固定缓冲尺度内死亡。应区分低扭曲和高扭曲。

### 2.1 正则近静态区的 Harnack 机制

Einstein 圆约化的垂直方程具有形式
\[
\Delta_q\ell=\left(1+\frac14\tau\right)\ell .
\]
在受控基底几何且 \(\tau\) 有界的自由圆作用区域，正解的 Harnack 与梯度估计给出
\[
\sup_{B_{R/2}}\ell\le C_H\inf_{B_{R/2}}\ell,\qquad
|\nabla\log\ell|\le C_H/R.
\]
所以很小的正 \(\ell(p)\) 会在邻域内保持很小，却不会在该正则缓冲域中降为零。换言之，小 \(\ell\) 本身趋向于产生可展开的存活纤维，而不是纤维死亡。

### 2.2 低扭曲收缩核的 Hessian 代价

若纤维趋向固定点，同时
\[
\tau=\ell^2|F|^2\to0,
\]
则 \(R_{a4b4}\) 由 \(-h_{ab}\) 主导。典型的低扭曲商空间收缩满足 \(\ell\sim r\)，从而某些角向分量
\[
\frac{\Hess\ell}{\ell}\sim r^{-2}.
\]
于是
\[
|R_{a4b4}|^2\sim r^{-4}.
\]
四维体积密度在圆塌缩坐标中为 \(\ell\,d\mu_q\sim r^3dr\)，故
\[
\int |R_{a4b4}|^2\,d\mu_g
\gtrsim \int\frac{dr}{r}.
\]
因此纯静态或低扭曲的收缩核不能位于满足所有中心尺度
\[
\fint_{B_r(p)}|\Rm|^2\le K
\]
的好点附近。

这一估计必须理解为低扭曲、无抵消的约化模型；在真正光滑 NUT 中，Hessian 项可由发散的连接/O’Neill 项抵消，不能单独使用。

### 2.3 静态不相容给出定量亏损间隙

在固定正则约化几何类中，若
\[
\tau_i\to0,\qquad \fint D_{{\rm cal},i}\to0,
\]
可将
\[
\widehat\ell_i=\frac{\ell_i}{\ell_i(x_i)}
\]
归一化。由于 \(h=\Hess\ell/\ell\) 对此归一化不变，椭圆紧性会产生静态 Einstein 极限。校准迫使
\[
\Spec(h_\infty)=\left(\frac38,\frac38,\frac14\right),
\]
而给定的静态常特征值刚性只允许
\[
h_\infty=\frac13I,\qquad W_\infty^+=0.
\]
故存在依赖于约化几何控制参数的 \(R,c>0\)，使
\[
\fint_{B_R}\left(D_{\rm cal}+\tau^2\right)\,d\mu_g\ge c.
\]
所以在正则、受控基底的近静态圆塌缩中，校准亏损与扭曲不可能同时趋零。

---

## 3. NUT 不能用“光滑故 \(W^+\to0\)”排除

必须修正一种过强论断：一般光滑固定点并不意味着曲率或 \(W^+\) 在该点趋零。平滑性只保证张量有限，并不保证局部渐近平坦到二阶。因此不能普遍声称“所有平滑 NUT 都有 \(W^+\to0\)”。

可验证的 Taub–NUT–AdS 模型说明了正确机制。其 NUT 对每个参数都光滑，但当 NUT 参数 \(\nu\to0\) 时，
\[
|W|^2_{\rm NUT}\sim \frac{3}{2\nu^4},
\]
固定邻域中的 Weyl 能量趋向正数，而体积为 \(O(\nu)\)，故曲率均值发散。远离 NUT 的固定环带上，曲率可小，但模型极限为实双曲空间，
\[
W^+=0,
\]
从而 scalar–Weyl 校准亏损为宏观正量。该模型由此展示二分：

- 接近收缩核：曲率均值过大；
- 留在有固定缓冲的环带：纤维可展开，但校准亏损不小。

这支持所需机制，却不能自动推广为任意 NUT 的统一能量量子化定理。一般情形仍需证明一个定量的“收缩成本”估计。

---

## 4. 剩余的高扭曲备选

若靠近纤维死亡区时 \(h\) 被 Einstein 方程推向静态各向同性，而 \(W^+\) 仍接近校准轨道，则扭曲项必须填补固定的各向异性间隙：
\[
|Q(Z)|\ge c-o(1).
\]
由 \(|Q(Z)|\lesssim |Z|^2=\tau\) 得
\[
\boxed{\ell^2|F|^2=\tau\ge c_Q>0}
\]
至少在区域的一个定量部分上成立。因而一般圆塌缩只剩下如下可能：

\[
\text{无固定存活缓冲}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\begin{cases}
\text{低扭曲收缩：产生曲率或校准亏损；}\\
\text{高扭曲收缩：存在阶一的 }\ell^2|F|^2
\text{ 或混合 O'Neill 曲率。}
\end{cases}
\]

高扭曲不能仅凭“总拓扑控制”立即排除。源材料中的 Chern–Weil 分析只给出更精确的结构约束。校准 Pontryagin 密度满足
\[
\rho_+\to\frac{3}{16\pi^2}\qquad\text{于 }L^1,
\]
故特征质量随体积分布，而不能全部储存在有限个消失体积的 NUT 核中。对
\[
F_{A_+}=F_H+\eta\wedge\Xi
\]
有
\[
P(F_{A_+})=2\eta\wedge P(\Xi,F_H),
\]
以及
\[
\left|\int_U\rho_+\right|^2
\le C\left(\int_U|F_H|^2\right)\left(\int_U|\Xi|^2\right).
\]
在水平曲率均值有界时，校准体积密度迫使
\[
\fint_U|\Xi|^2\ge c(K)-o(1).
\]
因此若高扭曲圆塌缩存在，它必须以弥散的混合曲率、缩放 holonomy 或 Chern–Simons 通量贯穿正体积好集；有限个 NUT 帽不能承担这一质量。

---

## 严格可支持的排除结论

在具有受控基底几何的正则秩一圆约化上，可以得到：

\[
\boxed{
\text{校准好集上不存在静态或近静态的固定尺度圆塌缩。}
}
\]

更具体地：

1. \(\ell(p)\) 可以任意小；曲率均值不提供绝对长度下界。
2. 若圆纤维在某固定缓冲尺度内存活，则缓冲正规覆盖将其展开；在满足最大秩和覆盖正则性条件时，得到非塌缩图并产生禁戒校准 Einstein germ。
3. 若纤维在每个固定尺度内死亡，则低扭曲情形由 Hessian 曲率成本或静态校准间隙排除。
4. 唯一未被现有证据排除的是弥散高扭曲机制：
   \[
   \ell^2|F|^2\gtrsim1
   \quad\text{或等价的混合 O'Neill/Chern–Simons 曲率保持阶一。}
   \]

要无条件排除全部圆塌缩，尚缺的精确对象是固定尺度估计
\[
\int_U|\Xi|^2
\le C\bigl(E_{\rm accessible}+E_{\rm fill}+E_{\rm O'Neill}\bigr)+o(1),
\]
其中 \(E_{\rm fill}\) 定量测量在缓冲域中杀死短纤维所需的曲率/拓扑成本。结合校准给出的
\[
\fint_U|\Xi|^2\ge c(K)
\]
后，该估计才能迫使正体积好点具有固定尺度可存活纤维，或证明所有纤维死亡机制都付出违反好点条件的成本。

## Exact Task

Verify the following static circle reduction formulas for a 4D Einstein metric with Ric = -g.

For a static Kaluza-Klein metric g = g_B + ℓ(x)² dψ² with Ric = -g:
1. The Einstein equations give: Ric_B = h - g_B and Δ_B ℓ = ℓ, where h = Hess_B(ℓ)/ℓ and tr(h) = 1.
2. The curvature operator on Λ²₊ (Besse convention) in the adapted SD basis has matrix R̂₊ with:
   - Diagonal: (R̂₊)₁₁ = 2h₃₃ - 1, (R̂₊)₂₂ = 2h₂₂ - 1, (R̂₊)₃₃ = 2h₁₁ - 1
   - Off-diagonal: (R̂₊)₁₂ = -2h₂₃, (R̂₊)₁₃ = 2h₁₃, (R̂₊)₂₃ = -2h₁₂
3. Hence W⁺ = R̂₊ + (1/3)I has: (W⁺)₁₁ = 2h₃₃ - 2/3, (W⁺)₂₂ = 2h₂₂ - 2/3, (W⁺)₃₃ = 2h₁₁ - 2/3, etc.
4. tr(R̂₊) = -1 = s/4, tr(W⁺) = 0.
5. The calibrated spectrum (-1/6, 1/12, 1/12) requires h = diag(3/8, 3/8, 1/4) in the eigenbasis.

For a cohomogeneity-one model g = dt² + a(t)² g_{S²} + ℓ(t)² dψ²:
6. The calibrated spectrum + Einstein give a'' = 3a/8 AND (a')² = 1 + a²/4, but differentiating the second gives a'' = a/4 ≠ 3a/8. Contradiction.
7. The ONLY constant-eigenvalue static Einstein has u = v = 1/3 (i.e., h = I/3, W⁺ = 0).

For the twisted case g = g_B + ℓ²(dψ + A)²:
8. The modified Laplacian is Δ_B ℓ + (ℓ³/4)|F|² = ℓ, giving tr(h) = 1 - ℓ²|F|²/4 < 1.
9. Near a smooth NUT (ℓ → 0), twist corrections to W⁺ are O(ℓ²), so the static formula W⁺ ≈ 2J(h - I/3) holds to leading order.

Check all signs, factors, and index assignments. Verify against the known results: constant curvature K = -1/3 gives h = I/3 and W⁺ = 0; the Taub-NUT-AdS has W⁺ = 0 but nontrivial warping (so twist must compensate).

## Integrated Scientific Memo

## Verification memo

Fix an oriented orthonormal base frame \(e_1,e_2,e_3\), let \(e_4=\ell^{-1}\partial_\psi\), and use
\[
\omega_1=\frac{e^{12}+e^{34}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
\omega_2=\frac{e^{13}-e^{24}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
\omega_3=\frac{e^{14}+e^{23}}{\sqrt2}.
\]
Take \(\Delta=\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Hess}\) and Besse’s convention
\[
\widehat R|_{\Lambda^+}=W^++\frac{s}{12}I.
\]

The proposed formulas are not all correct. In particular, Items 2, 5, 6, 8, and 9 require correction.

### 1. Static Einstein reduction

For
\[
g=g_B+\ell^2d\psi^2,
\]
the warped-product identities are
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g(X,Y)
 =\operatorname{Ric}_B(X,Y)-\ell^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_B\ell(X,Y),
\]
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g(e_4,e_4)=-\ell^{-1}\Delta_B\ell.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Ric}_g=-g\) gives
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Ric}_B=h-g_B,\qquad \Delta_B\ell=\ell,\qquad
h=\ell^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_B\ell,}
\]
and therefore
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{tr}h=1.}
\]
Hence Item 1 is correct. Also \(s_B=-2\) and \(s_g=-4\).

### 2–4. Correct static curvature and Weyl matrices

The relevant curvature components are
\[
R_{abcd}=R^B_{abcd},\qquad R_{a4b4}=-h_{ab},\qquad R_{abc4}=0.
\]
Since \(B\) is three-dimensional, \(\operatorname{Ric}_B=h-I\), \(s_B=-2\), and \(\operatorname{tr}h=1\), one obtains
\[
\boxed{
\widehat R_+=
\begin{pmatrix}
-h_{33}&h_{23}&-h_{13}\\
h_{23}&-h_{22}&h_{12}\\
-h_{13}&h_{12}&-h_{11}
\end{pmatrix}.}
\]
Other sign choices for the adapted SD basis can change some off-diagonal signs by diagonal orthogonal conjugation, but neither the factor nor the diagonal dependence. Intrinsically,
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat R_+)=-\operatorname{Spec}(h).}
\]

Therefore Item 2’s entries \(2h_{ii}-1\) and off-diagonal factor \(2\) are incorrect.

Because \(s=-4\),
\[
\widehat R_+=W^+-\frac13I,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{
W^+=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac13-h_{33}&h_{23}&-h_{13}\\
h_{23}&\frac13-h_{22}&h_{12}\\
-h_{13}&h_{12}&\frac13-h_{11}
\end{pmatrix}.}
\]
Thus Item 3 has the correct scalar shift \(+\frac13I\), but inherits the incorrect entries from Item 2.

The trace statements are correct:
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{tr}\widehat R_+=-\operatorname{tr}h=-1=\frac{s}{4}},
\qquad
\boxed{\operatorname{tr}W^+=0}.
\]

The constant-curvature calibration also works correctly:
\[
h=\frac13I
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\widehat R_+=-\frac13I,\qquad W^+=0.
\]
Indeed, the resulting four-metric has sectional curvature \(-1/3\).

### 5. Correct Hessian spectrum for the calibrated Weyl spectrum

If \(\eta_i\) are the eigenvalues of \(h\), then
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)=\left\{\frac13-\eta_i\right\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)
 =\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right)
\]
requires
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Spec}(h)=\left(\frac12,\frac14,\frac14\right),}
\]
not \((3/8,3/8,1/4)\).

With the displayed basis and the simple Weyl eigenvalue placed in the first slot,
\[
(W^+_{11},W^+_{22},W^+_{33})
=\left(-\frac16,\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right)
\]
corresponds to
\[
(h_{11},h_{22},h_{33})
=\left(\frac14,\frac14,\frac12\right),
\]
because of the \(1\leftrightarrow3\) index pairing.

### 6. Cohomogeneity-one contradiction

For
\[
g=dt^2+a(t)^2g_{S^2}+\ell(t)^2d\psi^2,
\]
set
\[
u=\frac{\ell''}{\ell},\qquad
v=\frac{a'\ell'}{a\ell}.
\]
Then
\[
h=\operatorname{diag}(u,v,v),\qquad
\operatorname{Spec}(W^+)
=\left(\frac13-v,\frac13-v,\frac13-u\right).
\]
The calibrated spectrum therefore gives
\[
\boxed{u=\frac12,\qquad v=\frac14.}
\]

The Einstein equations are
\[
-2\frac{a''}{a}=u-1,
\]
\[
-\frac{a''}{a}+\frac{1-(a')^2}{a^2}=v-1,
\]
\[
u+2v=1.
\]
Substitution yields
\[
\boxed{a''=\frac14a},
\]
and
\[
-\frac14+\frac{1-(a')^2}{a^2}=-\frac34,
\]
hence
\[
\boxed{(a')^2=1+\frac12a^2}.
\]
This implies \(a'\ne0\); differentiating gives
\[
\boxed{a''=\frac12a},
\]
contradicting \(a''=a/4\).

Thus the intended incompatibility is valid, but Item 6’s numerical equations
\[
a''=\frac38a,\qquad (a')^2=1+\frac14a^2
\]
are consequences of the incorrect static curvature formula.

### 7. Constant-eigenvalue conclusion

Suppose \(u,v\) are constant. From the angular Einstein equation,
\[
k:=\frac{1-(a')^2}{a^2}
=v-\frac12-\frac u2.
\]
Thus \((a')^2=1-ka^2\), and differentiation gives
\[
-k=\frac{a''}{a}=\frac{1-u}{2}.
\]
Comparing the two expressions for \(k\) gives \(u=v\). The trace equation
\(u+2v=1\) then yields
\[
\boxed{u=v=\frac13,\qquad h=\frac13I,\qquad W^+=0.}
\]

Item 7 is therefore correct **within the stated cohomogeneity-one ansatz**. This ODE argument does not establish uniqueness among all static Einstein circle metrics with arbitrary three-dimensional base geometry.

### 8. Twisted vertical Einstein equation

For
\[
g=g_B+\ell^2(d\psi+A)^2,\qquad F=dA,
\]
one has
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g(e_4,e_4)
=-\frac{\Delta_B\ell}{\ell}
+\frac{\ell^2}{4}F_{ab}F_{ab}.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{Ric}(e_4,e_4)=-1\) gives
\[
\boxed{\Delta_B\ell-\frac{\ell^3}{4}F_{ab}F_{ab}=\ell.}
\]
If
\[
|F|_{\Lambda^2}^2=\frac12F_{ab}F_{ab},
\]
this is equivalently
\[
\boxed{\Delta_B\ell-\frac{\ell^3}{2}|F|_{\Lambda^2}^2=\ell.}
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{tr}h
=1+\frac{\ell^2}{4}F_{ab}F_{ab}
=1+\frac{\ell^2}{2}|F|_{\Lambda^2}^2.}
\]
Thus Item 8 has the wrong sign: twist makes \(\operatorname{tr}h>1\), not \(<1\), wherever \(F\ne0\).

The coefficient depends on whether \(|F|^2\) denotes the two-form norm \(\frac12F_{ab}F_{ab}\) or the raw contraction \(F_{ab}F_{ab}\).

### 9. Behavior near a smooth NUT

Twisted curvature contains both quadratic and mixed terms. Schematically,
\[
R_{a4b4}
=-h_{ab}+\frac{\ell^2}{4}F_{ac}F_{bc},
\]
\[
R_{abcd}
=R^B_{abcd}
-\frac{\ell^2}{4}
\left(2F_{ab}F_{cd}+F_{ac}F_{bd}-F_{ad}F_{bc}\right),
\]
while \(R_{abc4}\) contains terms of orders
\[
\ell\nabla F,\qquad (\nabla\ell)F.
\]
Consequently, twist corrections are not generally \(O(\ell^2)\), even if \(F\) is bounded; mixed terms can be larger. Near a NUT, the quotient-base norm of \(F\) typically diverges as the fiber closes.

Taub–NUT–AdS gives an explicit counterexample to Item 9. Write
\[
V(r)=\frac{r-\nu}{r+\nu}
\left(1+\frac{(r-\nu)(r+3\nu)}3\right),
\quad
\ell=2\nu\sqrt V,
\quad
b^2=r^2-\nu^2.
\]
Then
\[
h_{rr}=\frac{V''}{2},\qquad
h_{\mathrm{ang}}=\frac{rV'}{2(r^2-\nu^2)},
\]
and
\[
F_{\hat\theta\hat\phi}=-\frac1{r^2-\nu^2}.
\]
The corrected vertical equation is verified by
\[
h_{rr}+2h_{\mathrm{ang}}
=1+\frac{\ell^2}{2(r^2-\nu^2)^2}.
\]

Putting \(x=r-\nu\), near the NUT,
\[
V=\frac{x}{2\nu}+O(x^2),\qquad
\ell^2=2\nu x+O(x^2),
\]
and
\[
h_{\mathrm{ang}}
=\frac{1}{8\nu x}+O(1)
=\frac{1}{4\ell^2}+O(1).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\ell^2F_{\hat\theta\hat\phi}^{\,2}\asymp \ell^{-2}.
\]
Thus neither the static Hessian contribution nor the twist correction is small in the quotient-adapted frame: both can diverge and cancel, leaving a smooth four-dimensional curvature tensor. In particular,
\[
h\not\to \frac13I
\]
in this model.

This is precisely compatible with Taub–NUT–AdS being half-conformally flat in one orientation despite nontrivial warping: base curvature, Hessian, connection curvature, and mixed terms compensate. Reversing orientation exchanges \(W^+\) and \(W^-\).

## Final assessment

\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
1 & \text{Correct}\\
2 & \text{Incorrect; }\widehat R_+\text{ is orthogonally conjugate to }-h\\
3 & \text{The }+\frac13I\text{ shift is correct, but the entries are incorrect}\\
4 & \text{Correct}\\
5 & \operatorname{Spec}(h)=(1/2,1/4,1/4)\\
6 & \text{Contradiction valid, but corrected equations are }
a''=a/4,\ (a')^2=1+a^2/2,\ a''=a/2\\
7 & \text{Correct only for the stated cohomogeneity-one constant-}u,v\text{ ansatz}\\
8 & \text{Wrong sign; }\operatorname{tr}h>1\text{ under nonzero twist}\\
9 & \text{False in general and false for Taub--NUT--AdS near its NUT}
\end{array}
\]

The supplied scripts hard-code the incorrect \(2J(h-I/3)\) formula; their isotropic test cannot detect the error because both the correct and incorrect formulas vanish at \(h=I/3\). They also do not compute the full twisted curvature. Additionally, in `circle_reduction_weyl.py`, since
\[
F_{\hat\theta\hat\phi}=-1/\texttt{rho\_sq},
\]
its square is `1/rho_sq**2`, not `1/rho_sq`.

~~~~markdown
# Step 12: 原研究交接

状态：Reflect（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

本步依照 Strategist 的修正重新读取 Step 11 静态圆约化、TTCS 记录以及 A01/A02 的 Taub–NUT 与 toric 文件，撤回“纤维死亡必然产生正比例高 ℓ²|F|²”和“一般静态常谱只能双曲”的表述。`workspace/notes/step11_circle_reduction_anisotropy_and_fiber_survival.tex` 与 `step11_consolidated_status.md` 已加入替代说明；H²×H² 被明确记录为一般静态分类的反例，T² 极性与单圆静态性也被分开。

本步检索并实际阅读了 Geroch–Einstein 范数/扭势方程以及 Ricci 下界空间的等距商理论。前者位于 `Knowledge/objects/papers/Geroch-group-for-Einstein-spaces-and-holographic-integrability--97a50a94c55d--463361159051/object.md`，后者位于 `Knowledge/objects/papers/On-quotients-of-spaces-with-Ricci-curvature-bounded-below--69d51d8f1cb4--a3b29d91ef06/object.md`，引用键分别为 `petkou2015geroch` 与 `galazgarca2018quotients`。所得可靠结论是：正规圆商的完整范数–扭势系统包含一阶导数扭曲；四维 Ricci 下界传给带权商空间的是 RCD*(K,4) 与 Ric_q-Hessℓ/ℓ，而非普通商 Ricci 控制。

核心新计算保存在 `workspace/notes/step12_reduced_equations_accessibility.md`。`workspace/scripts/verify_rank1_reduction.py` 检查了电磁 Weyl 分解、Taub–NUT–AdS 的精确 E/B 抵消、约化迹方程及 H²×H² 静态谱；`workspace/scripts/verify_chiral_reduction_identity.py` 精确验证了 a₊=u-z/2、a₋=u+z/2 下的 W± Riccati 分解、Maurer–Cartan 关系和迹方向。两脚本最终均成功运行。进一步阅读 Ye Li 四维平滑化定理后，笔记加入了校准余量驱动的协变平滑化设想，并解释为何现有 full-curvature 小能量定理不能直接应用。

本步 TTCS 的生成与核验任务全部不可用，未将其当作独立支持。新结构与修正通过会话组消息 #259、#260 发给 A01、A02。

## 当时的后续问题

围绕 `workspace/notes/step12_reduced_equations_accessibility.md` 深入构造固定尺度可达性的数学桥梁。首先用固定的 Riemannian 曲率、Hodge 与取向规范独立重导完整 Kaluza–Klein 方程，逐项复核 E、B、W±、dz、div z 和手征 Riccati 分解，并把 Ric+κg=e 时出现的误差项写成可积分形式；当前脚本提供代数与模型核对，但仍需一份不依赖模型的几何推导。

随后发展带权测度 ℓ dvol_q 下的 Bochner–Weitzenböck 恒等式。重点计算 a₊、a₋ 的加权散度、d a±、有限维 Bakry–Émery Ricci 项以及截断函数产生的端部项，研究两个手征 Weyl 能量是否能控制 ∇a±、a₊∧a₋、|z| 或商空间奇化的某个尺度不变量。必须保留迹方向并寻找其自身的散度公式，不能再从小 |Z| 推出小导数。若出现无法控制的相消方向，构造精确局部喷流、共维一扭曲模型或数值约化解来检验它能否同时维持校准 W⁺、有界 W⁻ 均值和趋零重建尺度。

并行比较两条能力建设路线：一是从 RCD*(K,4) 商空间的三维正则点、纤维同伦存活与加权方程建立四维覆盖重建；二是仿照 Ye Li 的无非塌缩平滑化，对移动的校准 Λ²₊ 谱投影或手征 Riccati 余量构造协变正则化。明确哪些步骤仍需要从原始 Ricci 控制序列产生近似圆/幂零对称，哪些可直接在四维完成。把有效恒等式、失败模型、来源和复算脚本保存到 workspace；若任一路线得到真正尺度估计，再交由 Agent3 做广泛模型压力测试。继续保持 Explore，因为当前工作是在选择并构造关键分析机制，而非已有完整负支证明。
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 12: full rank-one reduction and the fixed-scale accessibility problem

## 1. Repairs to the Step 11 picture

The negative-branch collapse problem should **not** be divided into an established fiber-survival case and an established high-twist fiber-death case. Three implications used for that division are unavailable.

1. Orthogonal transitivity of a full `T^2` action does not make either chosen circle action hypersurface-orthogonal. Taub–NUT–AdS is already a counterexample in the exact Einstein setting: its `(psi,phi)` torus is polar over `(r,theta)`, while the Hopf circle has connection `A=cos(theta)dphi` and nonzero curvature. The rank-two twist quantities are scalars on a two-dimensional quotient; a rank-one twist is a closed one-form on a three-dimensional quotient. The degeneration-edge argument for the former does not annihilate the latter.
2. Small `ell^2|F|^2` does not imply a static limit. The four-dimensional curvature contains `ell nabla F` and `(nabla ell)F`, equivalently first derivatives of the scaled field `Z=ell F`; these terms can remain order one when `Z` is small. A Harnack argument for `ell` also presupposes controlled quotient geometry, which the good-point assumptions do not give.
3. The static calculation in Step 11 proves only a spherical cohomogeneity-one exclusion. It does not classify static Einstein circle metrics. The exact product `H^2 x H^2`, with the circle written in polar coordinates on the first factor,
   
   `g = dr^2+sinh^2(r)dpsi^2+g_H2`,
   
   is static with `Ric=-g`, `Spec(Hess ell/ell)=(1,0,0)`, and constant `Spec(W+) = (-2/3,1/3,1/3)` up to orientation. Thus “constant static spectrum implies W+=0” is false outside the special ansatz. The general calibrated constant-spectrum exclusion remains the projector/Derdzinski Einstein-germ result of Step 6.

Accordingly, the governing question remains:

> Does a positive-volume set with bounded centered four-dimensional curvature means and vanishing calibrated deficit necessarily contain a fixed-scale buffered covering chart, or can quotient degeneration and derivative twisting destroy every such chart?

## 2. Exact rank-one variables

On a regular invariant region write

`g = q + ell^2 theta^2`,  `theta=dpsi+A`,  `F=dA`,

and use a `q`-orthonormal horizontal frame and the unit vertical vector `V`. Define

`u=d log ell`,  `Z=ell F`,  `z=*q Z`,  `H=Hess_q(ell)/ell=nabla u+u tensor u`.

For an exact Einstein metric `Ric_g=-kappa g`, `kappa>0`, standard Kaluza–Klein curvature formulas give

`R_{aVbV} = -H_ab + (1/4) Z_ac Z_b^c`,

`R_{abcV} = -(1/2)[(nabla_a Z)_bc + 2u_a Z_bc-u_b Z_ac+u_c Z_ab]`

up to the simultaneous sign induced by the choice of `V` or `A`. In three dimensions this yields the electric and magnetic Weyl matrices

`E_ab := W_{aVbV} = (kappa/3)q_ab-H_ab+(1/4)(|z|^2 q_ab-z_a z_b)`,

`B_ab := (1/2)[(nabla_a z)_b+u_a z_b+u_b z_a-<u,z>q_ab]`.

The reduced vertical and mixed Einstein equations are

`tr H = kappa+|z|^2/2`,

`d z = -2u wedge z`,  `div z = <u,z>`.

The first identity makes `E` trace-free; the latter two make `B` symmetric and trace-free. Up to orientation and the sign convention for `B`,

`W+ = E+B`,  `W- = E-B`.

These formulas have two decisive consequences.

* The scaled twist amplitude `|Z|=|z|` controls only the algebraic quadratic term in `E`.
* The derivative term `nabla z` lies in `B` and hence directly in a chiral Weyl block. It is not lower order as `ell -> 0`.

The exact source formulation uses the Killing norm and twist potential. If `xi` is the circle Killing field, `lambda=|xi|^2=ell^2` and the twist one-form is locally `d omega`. The Geroch quotient equations express `Ric_q`, `Delta lambda`, and `Delta omega` through `lambda,omega` and their first/second derivatives (with signature-dependent signs). They confirm structurally that the complete system is elliptic on every regular set where `lambda>0`, but becomes singular as `lambda->0`; cosmological constant does not remove the derivative twist field. See `Knowledge/objects/papers/Geroch-group-for-Einstein-spaces-and-holographic-integrability--97a50a94c55d--463361159051/object.md`, lines 98–156, with care because its displayed conventions begin in Lorentzian signature.

## 3. A chiral Riccati factorization

Define the two one-forms

`a_+ = u-z/2`,  `a_- = u+z/2`.

A direct tensor calculation using the scalar reduced equations gives

`W+ = -[sym nabla a_+ + a_+ tensor a_+]_0`,

`W- = -[sym nabla a_- + a_- tensor a_-]_0`

up to exchanging `+` and `-` with orientation. Here the subscript `0` denotes the trace-free part. The antisymmetric reduced equation becomes

`d a_+ = a_+ wedge a_-`,  `d a_- = -a_+ wedge a_-`.

The trace modes are

`tr(sym nabla a_+ + a_+ tensor a_+) = kappa + 3|z|^2/4 - 3<u,z>/2`,

`tr(sym nabla a_- + a_- tensor a_-)= kappa + 3|z|^2/4 + 3<u,z>/2`.

These identities are checked exactly by `workspace/scripts/verify_chiral_reduction_identity.py`.

This factorization is more discriminating than the proposed “high scaled twist” division. The calibrated condition constrains a nonlinear first-order Riccati tensor for one chiral combination `a_+`; bounded full-curvature means constrain the corresponding tensor for both `a_+` and `a_-`. But neither controls `u` and `z` separately unless one also controls a trace mode, a gauge, or quotient geometry. In particular, large `u` and `z` can nearly cancel in `a_+` while surviving in `a_-`, and conformal/quotient degeneration can hide the coefficient geometry in which these equations are elliptic.

## 4. Exact checks

`workspace/scripts/verify_rank1_reduction.py` performs two independent tests.

### Static product

For `H^2 x H^2`, `z=0` and `Spec(H)=(1,0,0)`, so the formula gives

`Spec(W+) = (-2/3,1/3,1/3)`.

This exactly supplies the counterexample to the Step 11 general static-rigidity wording.

### Taub–NUT–AdS

For

`V=(r-nu)/(r+nu) [1+(r-nu)(r+3nu)/3]`,

`q=dr^2/V+(r^2-nu^2)g_S2`,  `ell=2nu sqrt(V)`,  `F=-sin(theta)dtheta wedge dphi`,

the script obtains

`tr H-1-|z|^2/2=0`,  `tr B=0`,

and

`E = diag(-2c,c,c)`,  `B=diag(2c,-c,-c)`,

where `c=nu(4nu^2-3)/(3(r+nu)^3)`. Therefore `E+B=0`, while

`Spec(E-B)=(-4c,2c,2c)`,

which exactly matches the nonzero chiral spectrum from the independent coordinate-curvature script. This check simultaneously confirms that derivative twisting cancels an order-one electric anisotropy even though a toric action is polar.

## 5. What the quotient curvature bound actually gives

A separate robust structure comes from quotient metric-measure geometry. If a genuine compact circle acts isometrically on a four-manifold with `Ric >= K g`, the quotient with the pushforward volume measure is `RCD*(K,4)`. On a smooth regular quotient the measure is proportional to `ell dvol_q`, and the finite-dimensional weighted tensor is

`Ric^4_{q,ell} = Ric_q-Hess_q(ell)/ell >= K q`.

This is exactly the weighted combination naturally inherited from the four-dimensional horizontal Ricci equation. It explains why ordinary `Ric_q`, base harmonic radius, and ordinary Harnack estimates were not available: they can degenerate while the weighted four-dimensional structure remains controlled. The source is Galaz-Garcia–Kell–Mondino–Sosa, `On quotients of spaces with Ricci curvature bounded below`, Corollary 1.2 and the smooth formula near lines 70–80, citation key `galazgarca2018quotients`.

The weighted `RCD(-,4)` structure supplies doubling, Poincare inequalities, heat-flow regularity, and measured compactness on the quotient. It does **not** by itself lift a three-dimensional regular quotient point to a four-dimensional noncollapsed covering chart, nor does it keep `ell` away from zero. Indeed a collapsed hyperbolic cusp has excellent weighted quotient geometry and arbitrarily short but surviving fibers. The missing datum is topological survival of the fiber in a buffered domain together with quantitative reconstruction from the weighted quotient.

## 6. Refined obstruction architecture

The available reasoning now separates three genuinely different failures instead of calling all of them high twist.

1. **Buffered fiber survival.** If a fixed-scale buffered normal cover unwraps a rank-one fiber and has a controlled harmonic chart, the mean-transport lemma carries the calibrated deficit and the Step 6 forbidden Einstein germ gives a contradiction. This conditional implication remains valid.
2. **Derivative twisting.** Even when `|Z|` is small, `nabla Z+u tensor Z` can be order one. In chiral variables this is the freedom to keep the Riccati tensor of `a_+` calibrated while `u,z` or `a_-` oscillate/degenerate. A useful estimate must control a derivative quantity such as `nabla z` or the full `W-` mean, not merely `|Z|^2`.
3. **Quotient degeneration / rank loss.** The smooth quotient equations become singular at `ell=0`, and weighted `RCD(-,4)` regularity does not imply ordinary three-dimensional harmonic radius. Fiber death inside every buffer can occur through a singular set whose effect is encoded in the metric-measure quotient rather than a pointwise lower bound for `|Z|`.

The curvature maximal function from Step 9 does bound the mean of **both** chiral Weyl blocks on selected points, since it bounds `|Rm|^2`. Thus the sharper analytic target is not a pointwise curvature estimate. It is a compactness/reconstruction statement for solutions of the coupled chiral Riccati–Maurer–Cartan system on an `RCD(-,4)` quotient:

> bounded local means of both `|W+|^2` and `|W-|^2`, vanishing calibrated defect for `W+`, and the exact/approximate reduced equations should either yield a fixed-scale regular weighted quotient region whose buffered cover reconstructs noncollapsed four-dimensional geometry, or force concentration of the trace/gauge modes (`|u|`, `|z|`, or quotient singularity density) visible in a scale-invariant energy.

At present no source found supplies this theorem. The literature search found the exact Geroch equations and quotient `RCD` inheritance, but not the needed coercive Bochner identity or reconstruction theorem. This is a precise new mathematical interface rather than an established result.

## 7. Model-level coercive possibilities

Three calculations now look worthwhile.

* Derive a weighted Bochner identity for `a_+` and `a_-` using the `ell dvol_q` Laplacian. The trace-free Riccati tensors are the chiral Weyl blocks, while `d a_±` is algebraically `a_+ wedge a_-`. A successful identity would bound `|nabla a_±|^2+|a_+ wedge a_-|^2` by the two Weyl energies plus boundary terms. The obstruction is the trace mode, which contains `|z|^2` and `<u,z>` and may require a normalization or a weighted divergence identity.
* Work at the synthetic quotient level: quantify whether a positive-measure set of 3-regular points in an `RCD(-,4)` quotient has a definite reconstruction radius when both chiral curvature means are controlled. This must retain fiber homotopy information; quotient regularity alone is insufficient.
* Search for an exact or approximate rank-one countermodel in which `W+` stays calibrated, both Weyl means remain bounded, but the quotient reconstruction radius tends to zero through derivative twisting. Such a model would decisively redirect the negative branch. Taub–NUT–AdS does not qualify because core-reaching means diverge and accessible annuli are uncalibrated.

## 8. Scope relative to Yau 26

All of the reduction above assumes a genuine local circle action. A Ricci-pinched collapsed sequence does not automatically carry such an exact action. Passing from bounded-Ricci collapse to invariant reduced variables requires smoothing, local covers, nilpotent structures, or a limit-groupoid construction; the Calderon–Zygmund spike blocks naive pointwise curvature recovery. Thus the full bridge has two layers:

1. obtain a sufficiently exact rank-one reduced structure on a positive-volume good set;
2. establish coercive weighted compactness/reconstruction for the complete `u,z` system.

Neither layer is proved. The fixed critical Ishida–LeBrun negative branch remains a valuable test problem, but the positive branch, dimensions at least five, and Lean formalization remain open. The present advance is the identification and exact verification of the complete derivative-sensitive reduced structure, together with removal of two false simplifications that would have sent subsequent work toward the wrong theorem.

## 9. A stronger alternate interface: normalized energy concentration

Reading Ye Li's four-dimensional smoothing theorem reveals a more concrete route that should be compared with the rank-one reconstruction program. Theorem 3.6 in `Knowledge/objects/papers/0911.3104-Smoothing-Riemannian-Metrics-with-Bounded-Ricci-Curvatures-in--fc5404da6e14--415cdf5be1eb/object.md` assumes

`r^4/Vol(B_r(x)) * integral_{B_r(x)} |Rm|^2 <= epsilon`

and bounded Ricci, and then produces a Ricci flow for time comparable to `r^2` with `|Rm(t)| <= C/t`, without a noncollapse hypothesis. The same source explains that Cheeger–Tian/Li good chopping can shrink an absolute-small-energy ball by a comparable factor to obtain this volume-normalized smallness.

**Step 13 correction.** The claim that Li smoothing is inapplicable because the calibrated bulk has nonzero background curvature is **wrong**. The dimensionless energy `eps_r = r^4 fint|Rm|^2 <= K_0 r^4` becomes arbitrarily small by reducing the fixed radius `r_0`, while the Einstein scale remains nonzero. Furthermore, the pointwise `C/t` stability gap for the Einstein defect is circumvented by an `L^2` Sobolev absorption mechanism: in 4D, Hölder + relative Sobolev gives `int|Rm||E|^2 <= C_S eps_r^{1/2} (||nabla E||_2^2 + r^{-2}||E||_2^2)` where volumes cancel, and for `eps_r` small the gradient term is absorbed by `-2int|nabla E|^2`. This gives bounded `L^2` growth, then parabolic MVI at bounded-curvature time gives pointwise `|E(t_0)| = O(delta)`. See `step13_smoothing_bridge_and_L2_propagation.md`.
~~~~

~~~~markdown
# Step 13: 原研究交接

状态：Process（当时记录，不是当前证明等级）

## 已开展的研究

This step began from the Strategist\u2019s guidance that Ye Li\u2019s smoothing hypothesis is satisfied at small radius r\u2080 on maximal-function good points, and from A01\u2019s Step 14 identification of the same localization question and withdrawal of the static/rank-one closure. The work developed in three stages.

First, I read Ye Li\u2019s Theorem 3.6 (lines 321\u2013329 of the source) and confirmed the Strategist\u2019s calculation: r\u2080\u2074 fint|Rm|\u00b2 \u2264 K\u2080r\u2080\u2074 < \u03b5_Li for r\u2080 = (\u03b5_Li/(2C_{BG}K\u2080))^{1/4}. Bishop\u2013Gromov under Ric \u2265 -3g extends this to every center in B_{r\u2080/2}(p). The dimensionless energy is small because of the r\u2074 factor, not because background curvature vanishes; Step 12\u2019s dismissal was based on confusing bounded curvature mean with unit-scale dimensionless energy, and is now corrected in the note.

Second, I derived the evolution equation for the Einstein defect E = Ric+g under the normalized flow \u2202_t g = -2(Ric+g): \u2202_t E = \u0394_L E - 2E, and (\u2202_t-\u0394)|E|\u00b2 = -2|\u2207E|\u00b2 + 4R_{ikjl}E_{ij}E_{kl}. The derivation uses contracted Bianchi div(E) = (1/2)d(trE) to cancel Hessian-of-trace terms, and substitution R_{ik}=E_{ik}-g_{ik} to cancel all tr(E\u00b3) and |E|\u00b2 reaction terms. SymPy verification confirmed the algebraic cancellations. The pointwise Gronwall bound with |Rm|\u2264C/t gives divergent growth factor (t\u2080/\u03b5)^{4C}\u2192\u221e, confirming the C/t gap is genuine.

Third, the TTCS verifier confirmed both evolution identities, corrected the claim that -2E provides net scalar damping (it cancels exactly), and identified the critical L\u00b2+Sobolev alternative: int|Rm||\u03c6E|\u00b2 \u2264 C_S \u03b5_r^{1/2}(||\u2207(\u03c6E)||\u2082\u00b2 + r\u207b\u00b2||\u03c6E||\u2082\u00b2) where volumes cancel. I developed this into a complete L\u00b2 propagation argument: for \u03b5_r small, the gradient term is absorbed by -2int|\u2207E|\u00b2, giving d/dt int\u03c6\u00b2|E|\u00b2 \u2264 Cr\u2080\u207b\u00b2 int|E|\u00b2 with Gronwall factor e^C over time t\u2080=O(r\u2080\u00b2). Parabolic MVI at bounded-curvature time t\u2080 gives sup|E(t\u2080)| \u2264 C*\u03b4_i with all volumes cancelling. Numerical verification: absorption coefficient 0.71, growth factor 1.03, pointwise amplification ~7.2.

The TTCS generator analyzed whether calibrated W\u207a forces H\u22650, finding H \u2265 (1/4)I+B (the magnetic Weyl). A 1-jet model achieves negative H for B diagonal with entry exceeding 1/4, but after smoothing all curvature\u2014including B\u2014is bounded, so H \u2265 -(C\u2032)I. In 3D, bounded Ric_B=\u2212I+H+C\u00b2_{sym}/2 gives bounded full base curvature, hence base harmonic radius and 4D KK chart.

Results communicated to A01/A02 via messages #263\u2013264. A01\u2019s Step 14 smoothing vs reduction comparison independently reached the localization question. Step 12 note corrected. All evidence in workspace/notes/step13_smoothing_bridge_and_L2_propagation.md, scripts/verify_einstein_defect_evolution.py, scripts/verify_L2_sobolev_absorption.py, and trace/ttcs/results/step13_ttcs01_*.md.

## 当时的后续问题

The L\u00b2 Sobolev absorption mechanism for propagating the Einstein defect through Ye Li smoothing now provides a concrete path to the forbidden-germ contradiction on the calibrated good set. The next work should verify, stress-test, and extend this mechanism through rigorous computation and model analysis, organized around three connected tasks.

(1) Verify the localized Li smoothing on a buffered ball. Read Lines 183\u2013335 of Knowledge/objects/papers/0911.3104.../object.md in detail, especially the covering argument (lines 331\u2013335) and the energy estimates in Section 3. Determine whether the proof extends to a ball with the all-centers hypothesis on a buffered subdomain, or identify the exact step where global completeness is used. If a gap exists, test whether conformal completion (doubling the ball to a closed manifold) or a Dirichlet boundary condition suffices. Write a precise localization lemma with explicit hypotheses. Compare with the Huang\u2013Wang local collapsed smoothing (Knowledge item fd31dbed4f1f) which assumes GH-model and maximal rank; determine whether our calibrated good-point conditions satisfy those assumptions.

(2) Stress-test the L\u00b2 propagation on explicit collapsing models. Write a script that constructs a collapsing circle-bundle metric near Ric=\u2212g with prescribed fiber length \u2113(r), twist F, and controlled Weyl profile, then numerically evolves the Einstein defect under discretized Ricci flow. Verify that the L\u00b2 norm of E grows by at most the predicted factor e^C and that the pointwise recovery at t\u2080 gives |E|=O(\u03b4). Test on (a) a nil\u00b3 circle collapse model, (b) a Taub\u2013NUT\u2013AdS annular model, and (c) a product H\u00b2\u00d7H\u00b2 model. For each, compute \u03b5_r, the Sobolev constant, and the growth factor. Report whether any model breaks the absorption.

(3) Propagate the calibrated W\u207a profile through the flow. The Chern\u2013Weil and Seiberg\u2013Witten identities hold for any metric on the fixed critical topology, so the mixed scalar\u2013Weyl inequality applies to g_i(t\u2080). With |E(t\u2080)| \u2264 C*\u03b4_i (from the L\u00b2 propagation), derive the calibrated near-saturation profile for g_i(t\u2080) by repeating the Steps 3\u20134 analysis on the smoothed metric. The key inputs are: s(t\u2080)=\u22124+O(\u03b4_i), \u222b|Ric\u2080(t\u2080)|\u00b2 controlled by Chern\u2013Weil + small E, and the same topological parameter A. Check whether the completed-square deficit \u222b(|W\u207a(t\u2080)|\u22121/(2\u221a6))\u00b2 \u2192 0 follows from the original deficit via L\u00b2 curvature evolution estimates plus the bounded-curvature bound at t\u2080.

In parallel, keep the chiral Riccati equations (workspace/notes/step12_reduced_equations_accessibility.md) as the language for any obstruction the smoothing exposes. After smoothing, the reduced system has bounded coefficients, so all derivatives of u,z,H are controlled\u2014this is a qualitative improvement over the original metric. If the forbidden germ closes on the smoothed metric, it completes the negative-branch proof (conditional on the localization lemma). If a model test reveals a failure, document the exact mechanism and determine whether it points toward a genuine counterexample or a fixable technical issue.

All work should be in Explore, as we are testing a promising but unproven mechanism before committing to a full proof.
~~~~
